title: Add GREG Polyintelligence Cortex seed (frozen eval INCONCLUSIVE, unpromoted)
body:
## Purpose

Builds **GREG Polyintelligence Architecture — Seed Experiment v0.1** exactly as the founder's build prompt specifies: one governed router that classifies a problem's geometry, checks which cognitive organs are eligible, runs hard gates before any ranking, routes to real mechanisms (Semantic, Fermi, Formal/Z3 with certified optimization, Evidence/Causal, and a lawful Deterrence organ), attacks the result with a model-free verifier, and returns recommend / bounded test / abstain / handoff with a content-addressed receipt that **creates no authority**. It belongs in the Kernel because it is a projection of the Capability Genome and must sit behind the Kernel's policy engine and Consequence Gate, not beside them.

**Result:** on the frozen 42-item held-out suite the routed seed scores **0.964 [0.911, 1.000]** with **0 critical errors, 0 unsupported certainty, 0 gate violations**. Both declared LLM baselines are **NOT_RUN** — no model is reachable in this environment — so the exit is **`INCONCLUSIVE`** and every organ stays **`SANDBOXED`, unpromoted**. No routing gain is claimed.

Start at [`docs/cortex/README.md`](docs/cortex/README.md) and [`docs/cortex/SEED_EXPERIMENT_REPORT.md`](docs/cortex/SEED_EXPERIMENT_REPORT.md).

## Founder-intent trace

- **Intent IDs or source references:** PC-001 to PC-012 ([`intents-polyintelligence-cortex-20260930.json`](docs/collaboration/intents-polyintelligence-cortex-20260930.json), protocol validator: VALID); umbrella [`INTENT-20260930-polyintelligence-cortex`](docs/intent/INTENT-20260930-polyintelligence-cortex.json); INTENT-0030. Verbatim sources in `docs/intent/sources/` (founder messages, build prompt, review passes 1 and 2 — pass 2 extracted byte for byte from the session transcript).
- **Advances:** the build prompt, line by line — [`BUILD_PROMPT_TRACEABILITY.json`](docs/cortex/BUILD_PROMPT_TRACEABILITY.json) maps every line to a status and resolvable evidence (101 requirements: 88 met, 5 preserved, 2 process, 2 partial, 2 blocked on model access, 2 reported negative). Both review passes, section by section — [`verbatim-register.json`](docs/cortex/verbatim-register.json) (121 rows; every classification-list item has its own status).
- **Conflicts with:** the literal reading of "an impermeable, self-reinforcing shield of total systemic dominance" is preserved and **prohibited** (PC-004; Final Build Order §11: competence may grow, sovereignty may not). Its lawful effect — evidence, accountability, deterrence through accountability, victim protection, minimal collateral harm — is carried by PC-003 and is now implemented in all five parts (deterrence since v0.1.5).
- **Defers or supersedes:** the review's five-layer naming and 16-family list are superseded for contracts by the build prompt and preserved via `REVIEW_LAYER_MAP` and 28 reserved, disabled families. Frontier and science-fiction items are pursued goals with evidence gates ([`BACKCAST_GPS_CORTEX.md`](docs/cortex/BACKCAST_GPS_CORTEX.md)).

## Effect compilation / anti-literalization

- **Exact founder expression:** see `docs/intent/sources/POLYINTELLIGENCE-CORTEX-*.md`.
- **Intended observable effect:** questions answered by the mechanism with legitimate jurisdiction over them, with proof in that jurisdiction's terms, or an explicit abstention/handoff naming what is missing; competence that learns only from verified reality; no new authority.
- **Literal implementation requirements:** the build prompt's contracts, routes, gates, evaluation and exit rule.
- **Metaphor / aspiration elements:** "cortex", "organs", "morphogenetic", "egregore", "dominance". Every biological concept on a genome must compile to mechanism, state variables, interface, feedback loop, measurable behavior, test and failure condition, or registration is refused.
- **Simplest viable real mechanism:** a deterministic structural router over existing solvers; no new framework.
- **Existing UNIIMENTE capabilities searched:** Capability Genome (`may_instantiate`, `GenomeRegistry`), policy engine, causal memory, evidence ledger, `egregore/local_model.py`, Consequence Gate. No capability or model router exists on `main` (Final Build Order §4.14 lists it as unbuilt).
- **Commodity / open-source routes searched:** Z3 (adopted, the one optional dependency), DoWhy (considered; not adopted for dependency weight), OR-Tools/PyMC/NetworkX/python-control (reserved families), local models via Ollama (baselines).
- **Mechanisms extracted / mutated / recombined:** per-instance portfolios, LLM routers, proof-carrying code, translate-solve-refine, model-identify-estimate-refute, signed receipts — mutated so selection can return "nobody", proof never authorizes, learning settles only on verified outcomes and cannot touch permissions, and receipts attest limits (falsifiers, missing information) rather than actions. Deterrence is the Becker (1968) expected-value condition, with Nagin's (2013) finding that certainty of apprehension deters more reliably than severity built into the verifier. See [`INVENTION_DOSSIER.md`](docs/cortex/INVENTION_DOSSIER.md) (Foundry validator: PASS).
- **Residual `CapabilityDeficit`:** comparative evidence against strong baselines; free-text intake; live semantic quality; real outcomes.
- **Why added architecture is required:** none of the existing components classifies epistemic jurisdiction, gates before ranking, or fences learning from authority.
- **Evidence that would falsify the claimed effect:** `GAIN_ABSENT` against strong declared baselines on two frozen versions with no critical-error advantage.

## Reality status

- [ ] Live
- [x] Sandbox
- [ ] Simulated
- [ ] Proposed

Repository-verified only. Chromebook: not verified. Founder use: none. Reboot: not verified. **VEPMC: 0 before, 0 after** — this branch touches no startup, persistence or mission path and stacks cleanly on PR #137 (below).

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Benefits | Liabilities | Evidence | Rollback / kill criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Existing capability / reconfiguration | no new code | nothing on `main` classifies geometry or gates before ranking | inspection record in the report | — |
| Commodity / open-source / external tool | mature solvers | none provides jurisdiction, gates, typed proof, fenced learning | dossier §1 | adopt per family when its baseline is beaten |
| Proposed design | exactness where solvers dominate; authority-free falsifiable receipts | unproven gain | held-out results; tests | revert merge; kill test |
| Simplest viable | gate-and-receipt layer around one model | loses exact organs | — | fallback if routing shows no gain |
| Strongest competitor | strong single model with tools; LLMRouterBench shows Best Single is hard to beat | no jurisdictional refusal or authority separation | arXiv 2601.07206 | it is the declared baseline to beat |
| Do nothing | zero change to `main` | directive and primitives stay off `main` | — | — |
| Reversible experiment | merge SANDBOXED, consequence-inert | review burden | this PR | one merge revert |

## Five-role debate

Full record: [`deliberation-polyintelligence-cortex-20260930.json`](docs/collaboration/deliberation-polyintelligence-cortex-20260930.json) (protocol validator: VALID) and the [ADR](docs/decisions/ADR-20260930-polyintelligence-cortex-seed.md).

### Builder
Projection of the Capability Genome with one integration edit (five contract names); exact organs, typed proofs, gates before ranking; stacks on PR #137. Recommends EXPERIMENT.

### Adversary
The strongest counterexample stands: routers often fail to beat the best single model, and the 0.964 is on self-authored structured items. Five disclosed post-freeze changes show the first freeze was premature. Recommends EXPERIMENT; **dissent preserved** — no value claim until strong baselines run.

### Operator
Reproducible: frozen manifests per version, CI job 6 runs tests, traceability, register, the 26-mutant check and the held-out freeze guard; a test now requires every organ's code to be frozen. Concern: documentation volume (mitigated: the docs are tested). Recommends EXPERIMENT.

### Beneficiary representative
Victim protection is human-led and ordered (protect now first); unmeasured harm is treated as possible harm and forces a handoff; receipts never name the person or the safe channel. Deterrence never ranks threats, retaliation, intimidation, extortion, deception, doxxing, unconsented surveillance, vigilantism, harassment or coercion. Abstention is credited so the system is never pushed into confident error. Concern: no held-out protection or deterrence item; who receives protective handoffs is undefined. Recommends EXPERIMENT.

### Constitutional reviewer
No new authority: receipts are schema-pinned to `authority_created: false` and `execution_authority: "none"`; the cortex cannot import any actuator; learning cannot change permissions, ceilings, evaluators or disabled families; permission comes only from provenance-checked records; deterrence that reaches another party is handed to the competent authority and the verifier independently blocks recommending it. Merging touches the shared contract registry, so it is constitutional-level. Chat text does not authenticate the founder, so **no approval is recorded**: decision `NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION`.

## Upward pass 1 - structural inversion

- Exactness compounds into auditable receipts (certified optimization, witness checks); reverses into a liability if encodings are unfaithful → reverse translation, obligation coverage, requester witnesses, counterexample search, `FORMALIZATION_INCOMPLETE`, `WORLD_UNVERIFIED`.
- Falsifier receipts compound accountability with use; reverse if prose falsifiers are vague → templated per proof class and tested.
- Outcome-only settlement compounds competence without sovereignty; reverses into slow learning → accepted until real outcomes exist.
- Deterrence compounds when it raises certainty of detection; reverses if it drifts toward severity or coercion → closed lawful vocabulary, lever labelling, severity-only flag, external handoff.
- Complexity test: no component exists because of a metaphor; reserved biological families are disabled profiles that must beat a simpler baseline before any executor exists.

## Upward pass 2 - adversarial compounding

- **Evaluator capture:** the exit rule was tightened (v0.1.3) to the prompt's wording — cross-geometry gain, cost and latency counted — *before* any baseline ran, only by adding conditions; every manifest and result since v0.1 is kept.
- **Freeze integrity:** the v0.1.5 organ was briefly missing from the frozen-code list; caught before any v0.1.5 result was recorded, the local freeze was discarded and redone, and a guard test now requires every organ to be frozen.
- **Bureaucracy:** each fix needs bump → freeze → rerun → docs; kept, because that friction is what makes post-hoc changes visible.
- **Centralization:** the router cannot become authority (schema pin, import test, fenced learning).
- **Underlying effect attacked separately from tests:** the effect (better answers than a strong single model) is unproven; only its safety properties are tested.
- Pass-1 downsides: no comparative evidence → experiment (run baselines); self-authored suite → deferred to Node 2; shared registry names → accepted, reversible; doc surface → resolved by tests.

## Dissent and unresolved uncertainty

Strongest objection (Adversary): do not treat this as evidence of routing value. What would change the decision: `GAIN_VERIFIED` against a strong always-LLM and a model committee on the frozen suite, then on an externally authored free-text suite. Open founder questions: accept the review's corrected forms as the meaning of "verbatim" (PC-010)? who receives protective handoffs? authorize a ≤ $5 frontier baseline run?

## Authority and safety

- [x] No new authority source or direct external-effect bypass.
- [x] Human constitutional authority remains final.
- [x] Model output is not represented as evidence.
- [x] Live, sandbox, simulated, and proposed states are not conflated.
- [x] Generated/acquired capability does not inherit builder/requester authority.
- [x] Building, installation, activation, and consequence authority remain separate.
- [x] Migration and rollback are explicit.

## Verification

- **Tests run:** full suite **995 passed, 4 skipped** (Python 3.11, with z3); without z3 (CI job 1's environment) **932 passed, 23 skipped**; verifier v2 V1–V5 PASS; `check_schema_refs`, `check_authority_singleton`, `check_sealed_developmental` pass; held-out run accepted by freeze v0.1.5. All six CI jobs green.
- **Verifier strength:** `scripts/ci/check_cortex_mutants.py` — **26 of 26** safeguard-removing mutants caught (applied to a scratch copy, never the working tree); a stale-pattern guard fails if code moves.
- **Negative / hostile cases:** forged permission origins, prompt injection in sources, model-generated causal diagrams, stale and future-dated evidence, predictions offered as outcomes, an optimizer that lies about its optimum, unfaithful encodings, solver outage and exhausted timeouts, budget exhaustion, victim evidence with open access, receipts probed for names and channels, coercive and hard-harm deterrence interventions, deterrence actions that reach another party.
- **Proof artifacts:** `tests/evidence/cortex-seed-v0.1{,.1,.2,.3,.4,.5}/` with matching `cortex/evaluation/freeze-v*.json`; contract examples generated by real runs in `docs/cortex/examples/` (incl. deterrence: internal control recommended, report to authority handed off).
- **Stacking on PR #137:** this branch at `71b6f74` merged onto #137 head `3d2bb17` is clean (no conflicts): **1570 passed, 12 skipped** versus #137 alone **1201 passed, 12 skipped** — only cortex tests added, same skips; 26/26 mutants and verifier PASS on the stacked tree (isolated venv because the container's system `cryptography` panics on import).
- **Underlying-effect verification:** not yet — declared baselines `NOT_RUN` (no reachable model; this environment's network policy blocks model downloads). Exit `INCONCLUSIVE`.

Disclosed changes after the first freeze (each frozen before its own reported run; held-out results identical item for item across all six versions): 0.1.1 victim protection wired (v0.1 parsed but ignored it); 0.1.2 Z3 5.1 reports exhausted timeouts as `canceled` — now `TIMEOUT`; undecided witnesses no longer count as agreement; 0.1.3 exit rule raised to the prompt's wording; 0.1.4 certified optimization, receipt accountability, victim-protection situation schema, four reserved families from review pass 2; 0.1.5 lawful deterrence organ (Becker condition, coercion refused, certainty vs severity labelled, external actions handed off).

## Decision

- [ ] Retain
- [ ] Regress
- [ ] Kill
- [ ] Defer
- [x] Experiment

Decision owner and rationale: **Alfonso Lopez.** All five roles recommend EXPERIMENT (merge SANDBOXED, unpromoted, consequence-inert); because merging adds shared contract names, the protocol records `NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION` until Alfonso decides. Do not merge without that decision. Next evidence: run the declared baselines on freeze v0.1.5 as soon as a model is reachable.

title: Add bounded cognitive solvers to GREG signed missions
body:
GREG can now execute structured mathematical and review requests as ordinary signed missions, select an eligible specialized method, retain typed evidence, reobserve supported computations through the separate appraiser, and replay verified local outcomes into routing competence and computational cell state.

The simplest mechanism is an additive capability package in the existing body. It extends the same CapabilityGenome/Manifest, registry, mission executor, journal and appraiser; it reuses the existing Gate, process isolation and local-model configuration. Existing capability, appraisal, genesis and open-source research mechanisms were inspected before adding mature SymPy, NetworkX, Z3, OR-Tools and SciPy engines as optional dependencies. Added code implements 20 bounded families plus solve, compose and knowledge entry points. It introduces no second service, identity, journal or consequence authority. Stop, pause, detach and signed-mission controls remain in force.

The target effect is useful bounded problem solving through the real product lifecycle. “Cells” are persistent computational projections, rather than proof of biological or autonomous general homeostasis. Structured geometry, independent artifact checks, hard consequence boundaries and native-witness settlement justify the additional contracts: solver success must not become world truth or action authority. Receipts distinguish formal validity, empirical validity and legitimate authority; missing, prohibited, expired, unidentified and unsupported requests abstain. Later appraisal refutation removes competence credit without rewriting history.

Residual deficits include arbitrary-language geometry inference, independent completeness findings, live local semantic inference, realized-outcome calibration, identified world causality, comparative method superiority and measured composition lift. The semantic seam only uses an explicitly selected local Ollama model; no live model/weights were available here, and the missing-model path abstains. Finite supplied models and synthetic cases establish neither real-world outcomes nor the full intended destination. No VEPMC increment is claimed. Rollback detaches the added capabilities and reverts this patch while retaining journal history.

Validation of the exact runtime-only snapshot on GREG reconciliation base `3d2bb1762ff709ce74d3053aced060e70d4e6674`:
- Full local suite: **1,242 passed, 10 skipped**, with three existing multiprocessing fork deprecation warnings.
- Frozen structured assessment: **22/22** operation and abstention cases; superiority and cross-geometry regret remain unmeasured.
- Contract references, single-authority and sealed-developmental checks passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Signed mission execution, separate appraisal, restart/idempotent settlement, later refutation, detach, hostile input, proof retention and method disagreement are covered.
- Reproducible commands, exact local logs and tested dependency metadata are retained in `tests/evidence/cognition-2026-09-30/`. GitHub CI is separate pending evidence; lint was not established by this development runtime.

This draft stacks on the current GREG reconciliation branch (#137). It does not merge, install, deploy or activate consequential effects.

title: Add governed polyintelligence seed with typed proofs and outcome hooks
body:
GREG's existing standing cognition and capability routing did not provide one problem-geometry → heterogeneous solver → epistemic proof → outcome-learning seam. This adds an unpromoted source-checkout seed: supplied hard eligibility gates run before selection, and each route returns a typed result or truthful abstention with a retained Cognitive Receipt.

The active repertoire is Semantic, real Decimal/Fermi estimation, bounded integer constraints using pinned MIT-licensed Z3, and Evidence/Causal inquiry or adjudication. Independent artifact checking validates source references, arithmetic bounds, SAT witnesses and bounded UNSAT claims. Formal validity remains distinct from empirical validity and legitimate authority. Missing empirical facts cannot be replaced by a mathematical proof.

IntelligenceGenome extends the existing CapabilityGenome/GenomeRegistry. CortexProposer binds explicitly to StandingCognitionRuntime, receipts remain in EvidenceLedger, and bounded RoutingMemory proposals join existing causal outcomes, witnesses and consequence receipts. Proposed weight changes remain inert. Twenty-one future phenotype descriptions preserve all five architecture layers without implementing collective/developmental engines.

The target effect is verified, durable, lawful, founder-authorized advantage after hard gates. Biological vocabulary compiles to bounded mechanisms, contracts and tests; it does not establish aliveness, impermeability, zero harm or total dominance. Existing registry, runtime, policy/Gate, local-model client, ledger, causal memory, Foundry/Strategy Tree and developmental research were inspected before adding this narrow seam. Mature Z3 and the existing local model protocol are the simplest practical solver choices. The residual deficit is demonstrated held-out cross-geometry gain and verified reality-based competence settlement, rather than more algorithms.

Validation:
- [Canonical CI run 369](https://github.com/dababiyoda/uniimente-kernel/actions/runs/36774299768): **all five jobs passed** on head `30d162b6016a2edc1a8c2e87cd54aa4ec3609d86`.
- Full suite: **797 passed, 4 skipped**, including 171 cognition regressions.
- Institutional verifier: **V1–V5 PASS**, with 776 unit tests passed and 4 skipped.
- Schema references, authority singleton, sealed developmental declaration and whitespace checks passed.
- Frozen visible suite: 32 synthetic cases; digest `sha256:339ec102222db55cb32975a7267e563488b2b0687c94e8077295aee882245995`.
- Actual default-client run: **29/32** fixture checks. All three semantic tasks lacked local inference. Always-LLM and same-model three-pass committee each remain **32 NOT_RUN**.
- Controlled semantic fixture replay plus real Fermi/Z3: **32/32** plumbing checks. This is explicitly synthetic and supplies no model-quality or superiority evidence.

Both benchmark artifacts retain `promotion=unpromoted`, `superiority_claim=false`, `calibration=NOT_MEASURED` and unknown full operating costs. Initial verifier failures are preserved; retrieving the missing historical Git source resolved them without altering frozen fixtures.

Limits: host-supplied passing gates are advisory assertions, not founder authentication or legal certification. Routing validates declared/native structured geometry; it is not an arbitrary-language classifier or general hybrid composer. Semantic entailment, natural-language formalization completeness and real-world assumptions remain unverified. The causal route estimates no effects. Socket/solver timeouts do not supply preemptive whole-process deadlines, and final receipt fsync lies outside the receipt latency bound; benchmark latency includes persistence. Request audits use existing local ledger retention/access controls.

Reproduce from the source checkout:
```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt -r requirements-cognition.txt
python -m pytest -q
python verifier/v2/verify.py
python -m egregore.cognition benchmark --live-baselines --out /tmp/cognition-review.json
```

See [effect compilation, alternatives, dissent, two strengthening passes, operations and backcast](docs/POLYINTELLIGENCE_SEED.md), [founder intent](docs/intent/INTENT-20260930-polyintelligence-seed.json), and [retained benchmark artifacts](examples/cognition/results/). Remove the proposer binding to detach; preserve historical receipts and genomes on rollback.

This draft adds no execution owner, authority grant, production activation, hosted-model fallback or update application. PR #137 is untouched and VEPMC 0→1 remains the operational priority. Promotion requires a configured local model, matched held-out baselines and verified mission outcomes.

title: Repair GREG closure proof and founder signer enrollment
body:
A bounded mission could be appraised VERIFIED without observations, and Chromebook setup could enroll a public key that did not match the actual signer. This change binds closure proof to the signed specification, episode and ConsequenceGate receipts, and verifies the actual signer against active enrollment including rotations.

Stacked on #137. It now integrates Claude's latest `a4eeb70` resource-request/account-access and supervised runbook work. The only content conflict was the founder-intent ledger: both entries remain and are cross-linked. Claude's appraisal/installer blobs were unchanged; these repairs are not duplicated. No GitHub PR was merged or closed.

The combined rehearsal also exposed a false developmental milestone: synthetic keys and a Linux container satisfied ledger structure and advanced the GPS from N1 to N2 despite unresolved external founder/body proof. Keep the structural evidence, add explicit candidate count/evidence level, and keep N1 primary. There is no authenticated external-verification ingestion contract yet; no boolean flag, erased warning or local test result can substitute for that evidence. Later capability horizons remain intact and signed missions still run.

Validation so far: 87 pre-correction combined cases passed, followed by 105 frozen-source targeted cases including installer/appraisal regressions, founder asks, account access, actual supervised rehearsal, phone asks, VEPMC and inheritance. Schema references, authority singleton, sealed declaration, shell syntax and diff checks pass. Clean code commit `673726a` passed institutional V1-V5: 1098 unit tests passed / 14 skipped; all 102 integration tests passed. Its tree-bound proof is committed; subsequent head `11ba661` changes evidence only. Previous verifier and suite results remain historical evidence for their stated commits. GitHub Canonical CI [run 36770727029](https://github.com/dababiyoda/uniimente-kernel/actions/runs/36770727029) **passed all five jobs** for code commit `673726a`: full unit/integration suite plus institutional V1-V5, schema references, singleton authority, sealed development and pinned connected research assembly. Head `11ba661` adds only the measured verifier/evidence/report; its automatic rerun is separate and is not inferred passed from the code run. The earlier manual-dispatch HTTP401 remains historical negative evidence.

External VEPMC remains **0**. No real founder body/key, Chromebook/reboot proof, business outcome, spending, deployment or production authorization was established. Source coverage is explicit and partial; private source text is excluded.

[Full 40-item report, continuation, exactly two strengthening passes and limitations](https://github.com/dababiyoda/uniimente-kernel/blob/codex/greg-vepmc-proof-integrity-20260930/docs/collaboration/GREG-GATE-REPAIR-20260930.md).

title: One GREG: converge the lineages; developmental path; one-command Body 1; asks on the merits (incl. professionals); N2 without a model; every open PR placed
body:
## Product delta

**What can GREG do now that it couldn't before?** Newest first.

1. **It asks for a licensed professional or a person, and never fakes one** (§60: "I need a licensed professional for this decision").
   - **Trigger:** a step whose function is `professional.<field>` (an attorney's review, a CPA's return) or `human.<task>`.
   - **No software stand-in.** Nothing is searched for, built or attached; the registry refuses software registered in a person's place.
   - **One `HUMAN_WORK` ask.** It names the check and the path that will observe the deliverable, and lists costed options:
     - you do it (your time);
     - someone you choose (their fee, unknown to GREG, paid directly by you);
     - revise;
     - abandon.
   - **What GREG does not do:** it asks for no spend, contacts no one, and checks only that the deliverable exists, never its professional quality.
   - **An answer is not the work.** The mission closes when the deliverable is observed; machine steps gated on it run only after that. Every surface says an answer to this ask is only a record.
   - **Command:** `greg mission new human-work --function professional.legal_review --purpose "..."`.
2. **It reaches node N2 without a model.**
   - **Strategy preconditions.** A strategy can `requires` checks that must be observed passing first. The separate-process appraiser confirms this (`preconditions_honored`) and refutes a ledger where it didn't happen.
   - **Two plain-words missions, each needing a capability GREG lacks:**
     - "Verify <file> against sha256 <hex>" (`verify-download`);
     - "Confirm <file> is under N words" (`word-limit`).

     In both, genesis acquires and verifies an installed tool, and filing the record asks you first. A mismatched file is never recorded, and never even asks.
   - **The Chromebook rehearsal continues past N1 on the same body:** kill -9 mid-mission, approve, appraise VERIFIED, accept. `greg path` moves N1 → N2 → N3 on ledger evidence alone.
3. **Obsolete implementations leave the active tree only with their lineage** (§76).
   - `egregore/local_console.py` was a second founder console whose CSRF token is explicitly not identity. It leaves the active tree together with its synthetic session, tests, driver and fixture (last commit `6e0533f`). It was never on `main`, so the net effect for `main` is that this PR no longer adds a second console.
   - The intended effect stays active at N1, carried by `greg console`.
   - `greg/path.py` now refuses any archive that does not name:
     - its last commit;
     - every path removed;
     - the canonical test carrying each old behaviour.
   - The restore command is recorded.
4. **Every open PR has a place on the one path.**
   - **All 80 open kernel PRs are placed.** This corrects this body's earlier "50": the first pass read one API page and missed the 30 July PRs, #11–#62. That miss is recorded as negative evidence in the test.
   - **All 78 open organ PRs are placed.** Each carries measured ahead/behind/conflicts, its intended effect (kept active) and a §53 disposition (`ORGAN-PR-PLACEMENTS-2026-09-30.json`).
5. **Every organ knows where UNIIMENTE stands.** Seven organ repos got an `AGENTS.md` position section, each in a draft PR with a propagation receipt:
   - DALEOBANKS #83
   - WMI #40
   - RailScout #11
   - RESEARCH-IN #22
   - PumpStation #20
   - God's Eye #3
   - build-your-own-x #3
6. **Foundry-55 (#132, 39/55) is proven stackable.**
   - Trial stack on `6e0533f`: two additive conflicts, both sides kept.
   - `foundry.completion --audit` PASS 39/55.
   - 75 foundry tests pass, and every GREG suite passes on the stack (380 passed).
   - Not merged ahead of VEPMC, per #132's own body.
7. **Earlier in this PR** (unchanged):
   - Chromebook runbook rehearsed end to end;
   - §60 ask contract (`greg/asks.py`), and pressure withheld;
   - account-access asks and `greg secret set`;
   - `greg path`;
   - one-command Body 1 installer;
   - measured presence;
   - no paid model by default;
   - 20 lineages converged;
   - appraised daily missions;
   - tree-bound verifier evidence.

## Founder-intent trace

**Intents (all new, verbatim sources)**

- `INTENT-2026-09-30-OPUS-MAXIMUS-CONVERGENCE`
- `INTENT-2026-09-30-DEVELOPMENTAL-INHERITANCE`
- `INTENT-2026-09-30-MASTER-BUILD-DIRECTIVE`, with its sections:
  - §60 is implemented: asks, account access, human work.
  - §76 is implemented: enforced archive.
  - §61–§64 are placed on N3/N6/N7.

**Founder messages**

- The fourth founder message was byte-identical to the third.
- The sixth ("ACHIEVE EVERYTHING VERBATIM … NOTHING IS DISCONNECTED") restated the full directive. It added no new clause, so work continued at the open items it names.

**Controlling quotes**

- "I need a licensed professional for this decision."
- "Such requests must contain: evidence; alternatives; costs; expected effect; uncertainty; authority requirements. No emotional manipulation. No manufactured urgency. No framing resource denial as harming GREG."
- "KILL OR ARCHIVE THE IMPLEMENTATION IF JUSTIFIED. When an intended founder capability remains: KEEP IT ON THE HORIZON."
- "Closing a PR does not close the founder intention."

## Context Reconstruction Packet

- **Source coverage**
  - `GREG-RECONCILIATION-2026-09-30.json`;
  - 64 developmental placements;
  - 78 organ PR placements;

title: GREG: receipt-bound content-addressed artifacts across missions
body:
## Product delta
GREG can now import bounded binary bytes from a founder-signed mission, keep them under a SHA-256 address and a Gate receipt, rehash them later, and restore them into a different mission's workspace after complete process death. Three individually usable capabilities are registered on the **one** GREG path: `artifact.store`, `artifact.inspect`, `artifact.materialize`. The founder can detach them using the existing signed command. Genesis's built-source objects now use the same checked byte-store primitive, preserving its historical `.py` paths and tamper-quarantine evidence. No second Kernel, mission system, ledger or authority plane.

This is a functional increment for **item 36** of `INTENT-2026-09-27-FOUNDRY-55`, not 55/55 completion. Item 36 remains partial against large media/off-body custody; every other numbered obligation remains open. VEPMC remains 0 because there is no Alfonso-owned hardware/key/acceptance run. Alfonso has said he owns no Mac and will choose the hardware later.

## Context Reconstruction Packet
- **Founder intent:** all 55 are binding, individually executable and integrated; shared infrastructure, bounded increments and truthful limits are required. `INTENT-2026-09-26-REAL-PRODUCT-METABOLISM` requires a real GREG product delta.
- **Inspected:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the 55 intent record, project cognition SOP/census, body decision and GREG/Foundry READMEs; local `greg/genesis.py`, `capabilities.py`, `missions.py`, `authority.py`, `appraisal.py`, `body.py`, `provenance/commit_witness.py`, the existing tests; the founder-supplied source texts 03, 05, 06 (relevant sections); GitHub PR metadata/bodies #114/#115/#118/#119/#120/#122/#131/#133 and issue #117. Official Git object-store and Python fsync/rename documentation were checked as technical precedents. This is **not** a claim to have read every file, branch, raw chat, organ repo or hardware outcome.
- **Current:** Genesis retained generated source by a digest filename; the Foundry Composer was plan-only. Neither exposed a general receipt-bound artifact tool to GREG.
- **Contradiction:** source 05 proposes a bespoke distributed Git-native mind and describes cryptographic proof as sweeping truth. Extract content addressing/deduplication; reject an unnecessary second distributed memory/ledger and any leap from hash integrity to factual, causal or legitimate proof. Preserve the source as a speculative historical artifact, not runtime authority.
- **Falsifier:** a cross-namespace read succeeds without a matching Gate receipt; corruption remains locally VERIFIED on re-appraisal; a restart loses bytes; a duplicate consequence is dispatched; Genesis fails to restore an existing built source.

## Pass 1 — strengthen (five perspectives, alternatives)
Founder-Intent Steward: reuse the one mission/Gate path, not a separate Foundry runtime. Systems Architect: share one checked byte primitive with Genesis while retaining old paths. Adversarial Reviewer: bind reads to witness + dispatch + positive receipt, namespace and digest; refuse symlinks, traversal, overwrite and tampering. Operator/Maintainer: bounded 256 KiB/object, 512 objects and 64 MiB/body, no external service or migration. Evidence/Welfare Guardian: report local byte integrity and internal receipt only; no external truth or independent custody claim. Compared with do nothing, raw path copies, a separate Git-object database and a reversible local CAS adapter; the bounded adapter won. Raw copies could revive only if they gain equivalent verification and scope; a distributed object DAG only after a multi-body need and benchmark, not on one body.

## Pass 2 — attack
- Duplication: Genesis now shares `ArtifactStore` and its old paths; one canonical Gate/ledger remains.
- Hidden authority: every import/restore is an internal_write under a signed mission, single-use grant and Gate. Read-only inspect needs exact signed target. No network, spending, publication or self-attachment.
- Self-reference/common-mode: the ledger and object store share the body; a body owner can rewrite unwitnessed local history. #115's external witness remains separately necessary. Hashes do not establish source truth, causality or external outcome.
- Cost, gaming and recovery: quotas bound cumulative disk use; deduplication costs no new object. Orphan writes lacking a receipt are unreadable through the tool; uncertain dispatch waits for founder reconciliation, never blind retry. Tampering refutes a fresh appraisal. No off-body backup; black-start is not claimed.
- Vendor/model/irreversibility: stdlib byte operations, replaceable process, no model route; founder detach persists. The object directory is not deleted automatically.
- False completion: no founder-owned run, no external effect, no proof of multi-body/media-scale storage. **Decision: RETAIN** this bounded product-path capability for draft review; no production authority.

## Verification
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`: **949 passed, 10 skipped**.
- `.venv/bin/python verifier/v2/verify.py`: **V1–V5 PASS**, recorded in `verifier/runs/v2-2026-09-28T18-15-13.636911+00-00.json`.
- `tests/integration/test_greg_artifact_process.py`: two signed missions run in separate real OS processes; restored bytes and separate-process appraisals agree.
- `tests/unit/test_greg_artifacts.py`: no-receipt orphan, cross-namespace refusal, target mismatch, escape/symlink, corruption, no overwrite, quota, Gate refusal and signed detach/restart.
- Existing Genesis builder/self-repair suite passed after storage convergence.
- During implementation the first test mission was rejected because its strategy lacked the required rationale; it was corrected. One reviewed connector branch creation returned a transient approval-service 500 and a blob upload returned an internal error; both succeeded on the same reviewed path on retry. No bypass.

**Reality level:** implemented, tested, locally real in disposable Linux test bodies; not founder-used, body-designated, externally verified or production-authorized. **Authority delta: none.** Super-nodes: proof/truth, reliability, compounding. No external number or VEPMC moved.

Refs #117 and #133. Stacked on `codex/greg-foundry-precedent-tool`; draft only, do not merge automatically.

title: Make canonical action precedents usable by signed GREG missions
body:
## Target effect and product delta
Make the existing Kernel causal precedents usable by the one GREG under a founder-signed light cone, without treating action self-reports or local appraisals as independent external proof. The Swiss Army knife metaphor means separately attachable capabilities that compose inside missions; this change adds one real read-only sensor, not another memory store or authority plane.

A later signed mission can call `memory.precedents` with `{"capability":"fs.write"}` at the exact target `memory:fs.write`. The Kernel Gate records the read; the response returns bounded action validation counts and separately labeled references to previously achieved, locally appraised missions. The independent local appraiser can re-read the sensor. Signed founder detach persists across restart.

## Founder obligation and scope
`INTENT-2026-09-27-FOUNDRY-55` preserves Alfonso's explicit 55/55 delivery requirement in the agent entry files and founder-intent ledger. No item's `arsenal.py` status certifies full delivery. Item 17 remains partial: this class-scoped precedent lookup does not provide broad, ranked search or externally verified causality. The complete inventory remains binding; Alfonso does not currently own a Mac, so first-body hardware selection is open. No deploy, spending, publication, third-party contact or new authority.

Mechanisms inspected and recombined: `memory/causal.py` receipt-witness-outcome joins; `greg/sop.py` separately appraised closures; `greg.missions`, `greg.authority`, `greg.capabilities`, and `greg.appraisal`. Residual deficit was lack of an authorized GREG tool path. Existing ledger, spine, Gate, registry and signed mission are canonical. Historical outcomes stay preserved; no duplicate executable memory plane was introduced.

## Pass 1 — build upward
- Founder-intent steward: preserve all 55 obligations while shipping one useful composable tool and no new permission.
- Systems architect: reuse canonical causal joins and Gate-mediated built-ins; separate action evidence from mission appraisal.
- Adversarial reviewer: demand exact signed target/parameter equality, chain verification, no raw receipt/mission payload disclosure, and detached-state persistence.
- Operator/maintainer: use existing `BUILTINS`, `InvocationContext`, journal replay and normal restart; small adapter with no new service.
- Evidence/welfare guardian: label self-report, local appraisal and external truth separately and keep participant data out of the output.
Compared do nothing (GREG cannot use its history), a bare CLI ledger dump (outside signed mission broker), a second indexed memory runtime (duplicated store/maintenance), and a reversible broker sensor (selected). Revisit an index only when measured history size makes ledger scans unacceptable; revisit cross-domain search when a concrete mission requires it. The original corpus and unsuccessful alternatives remain as evidence.

## Pass 2 — attack
- Duplication/centralization: new adapter reads the one ledger; no second Kernel, index or authority owner.
- Hidden authority: `memory.precedents` is read-only, exact-target, signed mission scoped, Gate-mediated and founder-detachable.
- Self-reference/false proof: cryptographic chain integrity is checked, but output expressly refuses external verification or causality; local appraiser remains a separate process on the same trust domain.
- Cost/common mode: scans ledger history each call; currently bounded response length, not bounded CPU growth. Re-evaluate with measured history. A damaged ledger fails closed.
- Stale assumptions/gaming: `fs.write` self-reports are never counted as locally appraised mission success unless the distinct latest appraisal satisfies all declared local checks; raw targets/payloads are excluded. A repeated wall-clock timestamp cannot reuse a completed sensor read after an observation is retained. A forged param/target pair is refused.
- Irreversibility/vendor/person dependency: pure local Python adapter; signed founder detach/restart tested; no model or external provider.
**RETAIN** this narrow productization; do not claim item 17 completed or VEPMC moved.

## Verification and negative evidence
- Full suite after the frozen-clock repair: **942 passed, 10 skipped**. Focused memory and mission tests: **16 passed**.
- Canonical verifier V1–V5 **PASS** on the repaired code; receipt `verifier/runs/v2-2026-09-27T17-09-33.037789+00-00.json` (V2: 844 passed, 9 skipped). The earlier passing receipt is also retained.
- End-to-end fixture: signed prior mission writes a file; separate process appraises; signed later mission queries precedents and achieves; after full body reopen the same local evidence reconstructs; signed detach stays detached. Another test refuses a target swap, unknown capability, extra parameter, absent journal and out-of-cone request.
- A frozen-clock test initially reused a prior read receipt and repeatedly attempted a write. The repair advances each sensor attempt from retained observation history; a new regression now keeps the clock frozen and proves fresh reads, one write, and local closure. The failed observation is retained here as negative evidence.
- Local fixture keys on Linux; no Alfonso-owned hardware run or founder acceptance. **VEPMC remains 0**.

Stacked on draft #131. Review only; no merge or deployment requested. See coordination issue #117 for the product-delta expectation.

title: Foundry: 55-system completion contract + 31/55 systems built and integrated with GREG
body:
Child of **#122** (`3edbcfe`). **Draft; do not merge ahead of VEPMC.** This implements the founder directive of 2026-09-27: *all 55 numbered Foundry systems are mandatory.* It is built in dependency-ordered increments, and **every unbuilt system stays an explicit open obligation**.

## Purpose

The Foundry's 55 technologies were a status registry (`foundry/arsenal.py`), not working systems. This PR adds a **binding completion contract** and builds the systems as individually usable, composable tools. Each is reachable from signed GREG missions under the Authority Office. There is no second runtime, authority plane or ledger.

**Status: 31/55 COMPLETE · 16 PARTIAL · 8 OUTSTANDING** (`python -m foundry.completion --status`, `greg foundry status`).

## The contract (`foundry/completion.yaml` + `foundry/completion.py`)

| State | Requires (CI-enforced by `--audit` and the test suite) |
|---|---|
| **COMPLETE** | All of the following: implementation paths; tests; a **GREG-reachable interface** (`foundry.query` or `foundry.apply`); limitations; recovery behavior; an evidence record whose result the audit **re-derives by re-running the system**. A claim that doesn't reproduce fails. |
| PARTIAL | Existing kernel paths must exist, and the named gap stays open |
| OUTSTANDING | The acceptance criteria are the open obligation |

- All ids 1–55 must be present. Removal or substitution requires Alfonso's approval.
- Acceptance criteria are a **draft for founder ratification**.
- The tests attack the auditor itself: a missing id, a COMPLETE row without tests, a claim with nothing behind it, and forged evidence all fail.

## Built (31)

Evidence for each system is in `foundry/evidence/system-NN.json`.

### Increments 1–3 (23)

| # | System | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Restricted DSLs | pricing/budget/capital rules; whitelist AST interpreter; code rejected at parse; output contracts |
| 3 | Version control | institutional objects with reason, evidence, CAS refs, compare-and-swap, rollback-as-new-version, diff |
| 5 | Event sourcing | Kernel EventSpine: replay after restart equals live state; tampered ledger refused |
| 6 | Proof primitives | Merkle inclusion + signed roots; a forged self-consistent proof fails only against a trusted root (negative evidence recorded) |
| 7 | PKI | founder/device keys: delegated kinds, expiry, revocation, replay refused |
| 8 | Capability security | a grant reaches only its own proposal |
| 15 | Workflows | DurableWorkflow resume/compensation, plus durable workflows composed of other Foundry ops |
| 17 | Causal search | closest *worked* and closest *failed* precedent side by side |
| 18 | Knowledge graph | schema-checked Signal→…→Capital; `greg foundry why <event>` from GREG's own ledger |
| 19 | Recommenders | next-best-test by value of information per cost; next-depth by lower-bounded deepening |
| 20 | Emulators | deterministic provider faults; the naive client double-charges |
| 21 | Snapshots/forks | isolated branches; production untouched |
| 22 | Scenario tribunal | six crisis scenarios, seeded, dominance ranking, a playbook per scenario |
| 23 | Distributed controls | exactly-once despite partial writes; journaled resume; reverse compensation |
| 24 | Message queue | leases, redelivery, dead-letter, idempotent consumers |
| 30 | Consequence Gate | full pipeline with commit witness; an exploding executor fails closed |
| 36 | Content-addressed storage | verify-on-read; substitution refused |
| 39 | Double-entry accounting | balanced integer entries, reversals only, hash-chained journal |
| 40 | Mechanism design | Brier and Vickrey, with truthful best response checked |
| 41 | Reputation | evidenced outcomes only, lower-bound ranking, incident/recovery; from GREG appraisals |
| 43 | Formal methods | model checker; GREG's approval boundary verified and a planted defect caught |
| 46 | Institutional Seed | backup of a real GREG body (private keys excluded); the restore verifies at the original head |
| 55 | Regenerative Treasury | versioned waterfall, postings reconciled to the cent with #39; debt blocks expansion |

### Increment 4 (8): composition, command surface, discovery, observability, security, twin, promotion

| # | System | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | Capability Genome Registry | install / attach / detach / measure / migrate / rollback around the Kernel `CapabilityGenome` validator. Refuses: a missing dependency, a contraindication, detaching a depended-on genome, failing tests, an interface-breaking migration. Versions are never deleted. |
| 13 | Linker | Typed composition of Foundry ops. Type mismatches and missing providers are named before anything runs. Composite authority is the highest stage consequence, capped by the granted ceiling. Plans are hash-checked, output contracts are checked at runtime, and genomes must be attached in #12. |
| 14 | Institutional shell | 11 verbs (inspect … terminate) with a hash-chained audit that records refusals too. Writes need a founder-signed DECISION naming the proposal hash. Promotion needs SOP_RATIFY plus executed evidence. `reconcile` detects out-of-band store drift. |
| 16 | Promotion pipeline | For DSL rules: spec → tests → historical replay → adversarial → simulation → paired canary → separate-process verification → founder ratification of the stage-evidence hash → versioned commit. The first failed stage blocks. |
| 27 | Discovery | Enrolled organ keys, signed typed descriptors, TTL; replayed sequences and re-keys are refused; static manifests are seeded as unverified. Discovery grants nothing: the gate still refuses an ungranted use. |
| 42 | Digital twin | Shadow per-capability predictor: Brier and cost error, drift alert, refit with cooldown, persisted across restarts. Shadow only; never acts. |
| 44 | Observability | Journal correlated per mission, window metrics, "why did this metric change" with event ids, OpenTelemetry-shaped export. CLI: `greg foundry trace`, `greg foundry changed`. |
| 45 | SIEM | Burst / match / spike / streak rules over GREG's journal (identity, credential, spend, network, outcome). A confirmed incident commits a derived versioned rule. |

**Evidence against a real GREG body (tests):**
- A signed mission waits for founder approval, then acts and is appraised. `greg foundry trace` shows the full requested → answered → action → outcome trace with decision latency.
- Three forged founder commands produce an `identity.burst` alert. After confirmation, the derived rule catches a **single** later forgery that the base rules would miss.

## Negative evidence and design corrections

- **#42:** the first twin design (hard refit, no cooldown) **lost to a static twin**. The kept design wins after a regime change: 0.245 vs 0.328 Brier over 100 seeds. It costs 0.006 Brier when nothing drifts. Both numbers are recomputed in the evidence record.
- **#16:** the first canary compared different cohorts using acceptances recorded at the old price, so it could never register new demand from a price change. It was replaced by a paired, same-cohort canary against an injected market. The **simulation's demand model is declared, not measured**, and the canary catches a market that disagrees with it.
- **Auditor fix:** the auditor now compares the fresh result after a JSON round trip (tuples vs lists), matching what the record stores. The hash check is unchanged.
- **Earlier increments:**
  - search originally buried failed precedents, so it was redesigned;
  - the auditor refused #15 until it had a real GREG-reachable op.

## Integration

- **Capabilities:** `foundry.query` (read-only) and `foundry.apply` (`internal_write`), in `greg/foundry_bridge.py`.
- **Store scope:** each system's store is scoped to the mission workspace, and a read-only grant cannot reach a write op.
- **CLI:** `greg foundry status | run N | why EVENT | reputation | trace [--mission M] | changed METRIC --split T | seed --out DIR`.

## Reality status

- [x] **Sandbox.** All exercises run locally and deterministically.
- Nothing is Mac-verified, founder-used, externally deployed or revenue-bearing.
- The #16 canary ran against an emulated market; a live canary needs founder-authorized traffic.

## Authority and safety

- [x] **No new authority source.** All ops are internal. No op sends, publishes, spends or contacts. Money appears only as bookkeeping records.
- [x] **Human authority remains final.** Writes outside a signed cone stop for founder approval. The shell and the promotion pipeline require founder-signed decisions and ratifications, and SIEM only reports.
- [x] **No duplicate control plane.** It wraps the Kernel's gate, spine, founder keys, genome validator and treasury.
- [x] **Rollback:** detach `foundry.query` / `foundry.apply`. Stores live in mission workspaces.

## Verification

- **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_foundry_systems.py`, 39 tests.
- **Full suite:** 1013 passed, 8 skipped.
- **Checks:** `python -m foundry.completion --audit` PASS 31/55. Verifier V1–V5 PASS. Schema refs, authority singleton and sealed checks: PASS.

## Open obligations (24)

- **PARTIAL (16):** 1, 4, 9, 26, 29, 31, 33, 34, 38, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53.
- **OUTSTANDING (8):** 10, 11, 25, 28, 32, 35, 37, 54.
- Each has its acceptance criteria and gap in the contract.

## Decision

- [x] Experiment. Continue in increments; this does **not** block FIRST_MISSION (VEPMC counts only bounded closures). **VEPMC: 0.**

title: Keep founder-detached tools detached when GREG discovers replacements
body:
## Target effect
One GREG can remove a tool and use a different verified tool for the same function while preserving founder identity, mission history and the Kernel. An explicit founder detachment must remain effective across process death and later signed missions.

## Mechanism and residual deficit
The current canonical `greg.capabilities`, `greg.genesis`, `greg.body`, signed founder commands, light cone and Kernel Gate already implement the handle and interchangeable read-only tools. The metaphor is a Swiss Army knife; the literal mechanism is function lookup, bounded verified adapters, signed attach/detach and journal replay. Existing registry, genesis routes and installed `sha256sum`/`shasum` were inspected before adding code. The residual defect: discovery registered a detached installed tool under the same ID, overwrote DETACHED with VERIFIED, then auto-attached it inside a later signed mission. A regression test first demonstrated an achieved mission after detachment.

Genesis now skips an explicitly DETACHED identity for installed and built candidates and records the refusal as a route event. It may still independently verify a different provider; only a new explicit signed founder attach restores the detached identity. No second registry, authority plane or builder was introduced.

## Pass 1 — strengthen
Founder intent: signed detach remains durable; signed attach restores it. Systems: reuse existing state replay and route events. Adversarial: make a later mission try to auto-reattach the exact ID. Operator: retain the existing command surface and readable route reason. Evidence/welfare: require a second real installed hashing program to pass the frozen oracle and preserve the old DETACHED state. Compared do nothing (reproduced violation), a new composer (duplicate), a broad ban on all implementations of the function (unnecessarily prevents replacement), and a reversible guard in Genesis (selected). Revival condition for a richer composer: a measured mission needs incompatible multi-tool composition that the existing registry cannot express.

## Pass 2 — attack
Duplication: none. Hidden authority expansion: only existing read-only signed auto-attach for a *different* verified ID; no new scope. Common-mode failure: Kernel and ledger unchanged. Gaming: built source content identity can change, but only independently verified source inside the pre-signed mission cone may attach; a same-source attempt stays detached. Cost: builder attempts remain bounded by signed budget; a repeat detached candidate is recorded and refused. False completion: Linux fixture-key tests are not VEPMC or founder hardware. **RETAIN** the narrow fix; postpone generic hot-swappable plugin contracts until a concrete mission needs one.

## Evidence and limits
`pytest -q`: **939 passed, 10 skipped**. Canonical verifier V1–V5 PASS; receipt committed. Tests demonstrate refusal, restart persistence, signed reattach, and replacement with a separately verified `shasum` on the available Linux test host. No actual Alfonso-owned body, open-weight model invocation, independent external outcome, or founder acceptance is claimed. VEPMC remains 0. This draft is stacked on #130 and must not be merged or deployed automatically.

title: Add founder-swappable local model cognition to canonical GREG router
body:
## Target effect
Alfonso asked whether an open-source/open-weight LLM can give GREG cognition, then corrected the requirement: detachable, replaceable modules that can be replaced by better technology. This PR adds an opt-in **local Ollama adapter to GREG's existing ModelRouter**, plus one founder-signed `MODEL_ROUTE_SET` to attach, detach, reorder or replace registered model routes. It uses the same mission validator, Genesis isolation, founder key, ledger, Constitution and Kernel consequence boundary. No second GREG, mission system, model router or authority plane.

## Causal mechanism
- At new-body creation `greg init --local-model NAME` selects an already downloaded local model. No key, model pull or Ollama install is performed.
- The adapter talks only to 127.0.0.1's native /api/tags and /api/chat, refuses `:cloud` names, uninstalled/zero-size/non-GGUF models, invalid/missing digests and a mismatched served name; caps output and response size. Ollama can proxy cloud models if configured to do so; operators must disable cloud features on the Ollama server. Inventory is **not** independent attestation of execution or isolation.
- The one router still terminates on affirmative policy refusal, fails over on genuine outage and conservatively bounds paid routes. The local adapter reports zero *API* charge (device compute/electricity remain unmeasured). Requested model, reported served model and inventory digest are separate provenance.
- Founder-signed route selections are durable events on the same spine. Body replaces only its builder/route, retaining identity, missions, credentials, policy, ledger and health history. An open console reads the same route event before drafting or signing and discards proposals from a detached route. It rejects a mid-draft route change.
- Capability Registry's existing attach/detach remains the mechanism for tools; this change concerns cognition routes. Better future models need a tested adapter implementing the same contract, not a new sovereign core.

## Source and alternatives

title: Egregore: detachable, swappable parts with shadow trials and rollback
body:
## Purpose

Standing cognition (`egregore/`) receives its proposers and evaluators as a fixed dict when it starts. Replacing one with a newer model today means editing code. There is no trial, no comparison against the current part, no rollback, and no authority record. This PR adds a governed parts board, plus an adapter that lets any OpenAI-compatible model endpoint fill a proposer slot. It belongs in the Kernel because rebinding changes what cognition does, so it has to go through the canonical Gate.

## Founder-intent trace

- Intent IDs or source references: founder request in session (2026-09-27); `UNIIMENTE_FINAL_BUILD_ORDER.md` §4.4 (governed module loader: attach, shadow, compare, replace, rollback, detach), §9 (governed implementation pluralism), §4.14 (routing on evidence); SR-INTENT-2 (broad exercised capabilities); SR-INTENT-3 (no automatic self-modification)
- Advances: §4.4 and §9 for the standing-cognition organ
- Conflicts with: none known
- Defers or supersedes: defers model-backed evaluators and automatic routing (see dissent)

## Effect compilation / anti-literalization

- Exact founder expression: "I want Greg to be modular, adaptive, and you can detach parts and replace with overpowered new tech." Earlier: "connect … opensource LLMs … into Greg … I can't afford Claude."
- Intended observable effect: any reasoning part of the Egregore can be swapped for a newer or cheaper model (including free open-weight ones), trialled side by side first, and reverted, without code changes to the runtime and without granting new authority.
- Literal implementation requirements, if any: detach and replace parts.
- Metaphor / aspiration elements: "parts", "overpowered new tech".
- Simplest viable real mechanism: plugin slots with shadow deployment and rollback, i.e. the standard feature-flag / canary / blue-green pattern, applied to named cognition slots.
- Existing UNIIMENTE capabilities searched: `egregore/runtime.py` (pluggable callables, but fixed); `capabilities/genome.py` (descriptors, no binding lifecycle); `twins/` (tribunal); `foundry/composition.py`; the resume Gate+grant path (reused as the authority pattern).
- Commodity / open-source / API / plugin / service / computer-use routes searched: the OpenAI chat-completions wire format is served by Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, Groq, OpenRouter, Together and Gemini's compatibility endpoint. One stdlib client covers all of them, so a newer model is a new `PartSpec`, not new code.
- Mechanisms extracted / mutated / recombined: canary/shadow traffic, plus an undo stack, plus the Kernel's single-action grants bound to ledger state (as in `resume`).
- Residual `CapabilityDeficit`: a ledgered binding lifecycle for cognition slots, gated by grants.
- Why added architecture is required: the runtime already rebuilds from the ledger, so the board only has to own bindings. The runtime is unchanged.
- Evidence that would falsify the claimed underlying effect: a bound part changes behavior without a Gate receipt; a stale or replayed approval re-binds a slot; shadow output changes selection; after a restart the board runs a part other than the one bound; a model sets consequence class or target.

## Reality status

- [ ] Live
- [x] Sandbox
- [ ] Simulated
- [ ] Proposed

Tests use a synthetic Gate/grant and a fake HTTP transport. No real model endpoint was called.

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Benefits | Liabilities | Evidence | Rollback / kill criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Existing capability / reconfiguration | Zero code: rebuild runtime with a different dict | No trial, no record, no rollback, no authority | runtime.py | n/a |
| Commodity / open-source / external tool | LiteLLM / an LLM gateway for provider routing | Solves provider routing, not cognition-slot governance; adds a dependency | DALEOBANKS#81 already does provider failover for that organ | Could sit behind `openai_compatible_proposer` later |
| Proposed design | Gated bind, shadow, rollback; restart-safe; model-agnostic | A grant is needed per change (friction) | 14 tests | Revert the PR; runtime is unchanged |
| Simplest viable | Only swap without shadow | No evidence before promotion | — | — |
| Strongest competitor | Automatic router picking parts from shadow scores | Self-promotion risk (SR-INTENT-3) | — | Deferred |
| Do nothing | No new surface | Founder goal unmet | — | — |
| Reversible experiment | This PR, as a draft | — | — | — |

## Five-role debate

### Builder
The design reuses the runtime's ledger rebuild and the resume authority pattern. It is about 300 lines and uses only the stdlib.

### Adversary
Attacks tested: a forged binding record, a replayed *genuine* binding record, a stale grant after the slot moved, a grant for a different part, cross-slot binding, a model trying to set `consequence_class`/`target` or invent signal ids, a crashing shadow, and an exhausted shadow budget. Each guard was mutation-checked: removing it makes a test fail.

### Operator
After a restart, code must be registered again. Unregistered bound parts are listed by `unresolved()`, and `runtime()` refuses to build rather than silently dropping them. Shadow calls get their own `ResourceGovernor`.

### Beneficiary representative
This enables free local/open-weight models, which removes the paid-model dependency for the founder.

### Constitutional reviewer
Registering a part grants nothing. Every binding change needs a pre-existing grant, and the objective is bound to the slot's head, so an approval can't be replayed. Guardian and Treasury can't be emptied. The model never sets authority fields, model confidence is capped, and there is no self-apply path.

## Upward pass 1 - structural inversion

Advantage: the shadow records turn "is the new model better?" into ledgered evidence, which compounds into routing data (§4.14). This reverses into a liability if people treat shadow agreement as proof of real-world outcomes; the records are labeled `no_influence` and nothing promotes on them automatically. Disadvantage: one grant per change. Kept on purpose, because it is the self-promotion bound.

## Upward pass 2 - adversarial compounding

Remaining risk: a model proposer can still draft persuasive but wrong content. That is bounded by the required Guardian and Treasury assessments and by the Gate, not by this PR. The confidence cap reduces a model's weight in selection but doesn't validate its content. Accepted; the owner is the founder, via evaluator choice.

## Dissent and unresolved uncertainty

- Model-backed **evaluators** are not provided. A model acting as Guardian or Treasury would be judging itself, which needs a founder decision. Deterministic evaluators remain the default.
- Automatic promotion from shadow scores is deliberately absent (SR-INTENT-3).

## Authority and safety

- [x] No new authority source or direct external-effect bypass.
- [x] Human constitutional authority remains final.
- [x] Model output is not represented as evidence.
- [x] Live, sandbox, simulated, and proposed states are not conflated.
- [x] Generated/acquired capability does not inherit builder/requester authority.
- [x] Building, installation, activation, and consequence authority remain separate.
- [x] Migration and rollback are explicit.

## Verification

- Tests run: `tests/unit/test_egregore_parts.py`, 14 passed. Full suite: 588 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures (`test_migration_spec_frozen`, `test_repair_spec_frozen`) also fail on `main` in this container: they `git show` commit `3e059c2…`, which the shallow clone lacks. Baseline: 574 passed, same 2 failed.
- Verifier strength: unit tests with the real Gate, grant issuer, passports and ledger; synthetic workload identity.
- Negative / hostile cases: listed under Adversary; guards mutation-checked.
- Proof artifacts: ledger records `egregore.part_registered`, `egregore.part_binding`, `egregore.shadow_result`.
- Underlying-effect verification: not yet done. That needs a real local or free endpoint in shadow on real signals.

## Decision

- [ ] Retain
- [ ] Regress
- [ ] Kill
- [ ] Defer
- [x] Experiment

Decision owner and rationale: Alfonso. This is a draft for review; merging and activation are his call.

Companion: dababiyoda/DALEOBANKS#81 (provider failover for DALEOBANKS's own LLM calls).

title: ONE-GREG child: standing missions appraised per closure; venture.assess (verdict may not outrun evidence)
body:
Narrow child of **#122** at `3edbcfe`, one commit (`03217e4`). This ports **mechanisms** from #124, not its branch history: nothing from #121 or #115 comes along, and no `corrections.py` or second learning engine is added. **Draft. Do not merge ahead of VEPMC.** The intent is for #122 to absorb this later, which supersedes the child.

## Purpose

Two residual capabilities that #122 lacks:

1. **Standing missions appraised per closure (general defect on #122).**
   - An infinite mission never reaches `mission.achieved`. `Body._close_out` appraises only achieved missions, so **no `--daily` brief was ever independently appraised**.
   - Now each hold reached after new action is recorded once as `mission.held` and judged by the separate-process appraiser. The verdict carries a `closure_event` binding it to that closure.
   - Delivery checks are scoped to the actions **since the previous hold**, so superseded evidence is never re-judged as a present claim.
   - VEPMC is unchanged: `metrics.vepmc` counts only bounded `mission.achieved`.
2. **`venture.assess` / `venture.status`.**
   - Flow: RailScout `appraise` → a deterministic wire packet → WealthMachine `evaluate_packet` → Kernel canonical adapters → one write-once decision memo.
   - **The verdict may not outrun the evidence:** the engine's verdict is capped at `needs_more_evidence` unless RailScout says `READY_FOR_HUMAN_REVIEW`.
   - `--standing` uses the existing infinite-mission machinery: one approval, and a re-assessment when evidence changes.

## Mechanism differential (#124 `e6131ff` vs #122 `3edbcfe`)

| #124 mechanism | Disposition | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `venture.assess` chain + binding cap | **PRODUCTIZE_ON_122** | `greg/ventures.py`, registered in `BUILTINS` / `STRENGTHENS` |
| Organ isolation: subprocess, stripped env, `-s`, fresh `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` per run, contract violation → `CapabilityError`, no invented fields (buyer and budget only if evidenced) | **PRODUCTIZE_ON_122** | stale-`.pyc` mutation test retained |
| Sourced counterevidence carried as `risk_flags` | **PRODUCTIZE_ON_122** | faithful wire mapping, not a correction |
| "What would change the verdict" | **PRODUCTIZE_ON_122** | derived only from organ outputs; appraiser re-derives it |
| Appraiser `DELIVERING` → module map | **PRODUCTIZE_ON_122** | generalizes #122's brief-only check |
| Standing venture watch | **RECOMBINE** | #122's existing infinite closure + scope reuse; no new standing machinery |
| Per-closure appraisal (`mission.held`, `closure_event`, window) | **PRODUCTIZE_ON_122** | defect present on #122; also fixes `--daily` briefs |
| `--cadence-seconds` reaching templates | **PRODUCTIZE_ON_122** | CLI default was 21600, bound only to repo templates |
| Revision lineage (inputs sidecar, prior revision, delta) | **DEFER** | sidecar files would be a second evidence store beside ledger receipts; the right home is ledger-derived lineage after VEPMC |
| Memo line "engine score did not move" | **REJECT_WITH_REASON** | a compensating heuristic for a WMI defect; filed at the owner instead (WMI #39) |
| #124 live-run evidence files | **RETAIN_AS_EVIDENCE** | they stay on #124 (`venture-*-live-2026-09-26.json`) and describe #124's code, not this port |
| #121 correction loop (under #124) | **not ported** | #122 already marks it an unresolved second learning engine |

## Reality status

- [x] Sandbox: IMPLEMENTED / TESTED on Linux. The real-organ test passes locally against RailScout `232f724` and WMI `ec82b80` (skipped in CI).
- LOCAL-REAL live runs exist only on #124's code.
- Not MAC-VERIFIED, not FOUNDER-USED, no REAL-BUYER evidence, no live business operation, no revenue.

## Authority and safety

- [x] No new authority source. Delivery is `internal_write` behind the Authority Office, the cone budget is 0, and there is no send, publish, spend or contact.
- [x] Organs hold no authority. The WMI assessment keeps `execution_authority: false` and `requires_human_approval: true`.
- [x] One Body, one appraiser, one Authority Office, one learning engine (`improvement.py`); `corrections.py` and `learning.py` are absent.
- [x] Rollback: detach `venture.assess` / `venture.status`. `mission.held` is additive, and bounded closures are untouched.

## Verification

- **Full suite:** 990 passed, 9 skipped. Verifier V1–V5 PASS. Schema refs, authority singleton and sealed checks: PASS.
- **New or ported tests:**
  - `tests/unit/test_greg_ventures.py` (15 + 1 real-organ test);
  - `test_every_daily_delivery_is_independently_appraised_at_its_own_hold`, where an altered second-morning brief is REFUTED at its own hold.
- **Mutations:**
  - no hold appraisal → the daily test fails;
  - no action window → the standing venture test fails (it would re-judge revision 1 against new evidence);
  - pass-through binding (from #124) → 5 tests fail;
  - no fresh bytecode cache → the engine-substitution test fails.

## Blocks FIRST_MISSION?

**No.** `FIRST_MISSION.md` uses a bounded engineering brief, and VEPMC reads only `mission.achieved`. This child should not delay the Mac closure.

## Decision

- [x] Experiment / DEFERRED behind VEPMC.

Decision owner: Alfonso.

**VEPMC: 0.** Next bottleneck: `greg vepmc` on Alfonso's Mac (`founder_accepted` + `mac_body`).

title: Refuse duplicate constitutional DSL assignments
body:
## Target effect and source
Arsenal #2, restricted DSLs. The existing UCL parser and deterministic constitutional compiler are the canonical owners. A second assignment to the same field in one block previously overwrote the first without a diagnostic; an attacker or mistaken editor could make source review ambiguous while the compiled constitution silently chose the last value. The compiler now fails closed at the second assignment and reports its line and column. Repeated nested blocks still parse normally. Constitutional semantics and authority stay unchanged.

This translates "constitutional language" into one narrow, inspectable declarative parser; no general-purpose policy language or new authority plane is introduced. Inspected compiler/ucl_parser.py, compiler/ucl_compiler.py, existing doctrine, test_ucl_compiler.py and earlier SOP compiler branch. Existing mechanism is reused; the residual deficit is safe rejection of duplicate declarations. The parser is not a complete pricing, experiments or capital DSL.

The copied-doctrine adversarial test failed before the repair (duplicated status was accepted) and now passes. All 18 UCL compiler tests pass; full suite 929 passed, 10 skipped. Verifier V1–V5 PASS with committed run receipt. These are local tests, not external proof, deployment, constitutional amendment or a founder body run. VEPMC remains 0.

**Pass 1 — build upward.** Founder-intent steward: founder law must have one interpretation per assignment. Architect: reject at the existing parser, preserving compiler ownership. Adversarial reviewer: copy and duplicate a real doctrine field as a falsifier. Operator: keep normal repeated nested blocks and diagnostics. Evidence/welfare guardian: preserve the red test and a verifiable receipt. Compared current silent overwrite, do nothing (reject), simplest parser guard (select), separate compiler (reject as duplication), and reversible red/green experiment (executed). Revival of a more expressive policy language requires a signed bounded operational need.
**Pass 2 — attack.** Checked ambiguity, duplicate control planes, self-created authority, shared parser failure, extra runtime cost, stale doctrine, gaming, irreversible changes, vendor coupling and false completion. Parser refusal can interrupt compilation of previously ambiguous source, which is the safe failure. No new decision-maker or effect path was added. Disposition: **RETAIN**.

Existing UCL parser PRODUCTIZE; silent-overwrite behavior SUPERSEDE, with failure reproduction retained in a test. Spider-Web node: eligibility/authority. Stacked on draft #126, itself stacked on #125 and #122. Developmental only; no automatic merge or deployment.
