title: verifier: bind run records to the tree they measure (Finding 3 repair proposal)
body:
## Purpose

Bind every verifier run record to the tree it measured. Today a run record carries no commit binding, so a record written against a partial or stale mirror can sit atop canonical history and read as if it described it. This is Finding 3 of the independent audit (`docs/audit/INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_8cb3074a.md`, PR #83): main tip `542c8f57` adds a 172-test / 13-module / partial-mirror-skip record above the canonical-v1 merge — honest (its `skips` field discloses) but unbound to what it measured. This PR implements the report's recommendation as a small, separable change: records embed `head_commit` = `git rev-parse HEAD` when a git object store exists, else `MIRROR_UNKNOWN`.

Affected boundary: `verifier/run_binding.py` (new), `verifier/verify.py` and `verifier/v2/verify.py` (one import + one record field each), `tests/unit/test_run_record_head_binding.py` (new, 5 tests), plus two demonstration run records. No behavior change to any check; the verifiers' verdicts are untouched.

## Founder-intent trace

- Source: independent audit Finding 3 (PR #83) → founder decision item in issue #84; standing founder directive that run records preserve the full trajectory, including unpublished and failing runs
- Advances: proof-before-expansion — a record that cannot name its subject tree is weaker evidence; this makes the weakness impossible to hide
- Conflicts with: none recorded
- Defers: formally deprecating standalone v1 (issue #84 item 1) and any re-recording of historical records (append-only; untouched here)

## Reality status

- [ ] Live
- [ ] Sandbox
- [ ] Simulated
- [x] Proposed

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Benefits | Liabilities | Evidence | Rollback / kill criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Proposed design (shared `run_binding.py`, fail-closed `MIRROR_UNKNOWN`) | One helper, both verifiers; honest degradation on mirrors; 5 lock tests | New field consumers must tolerate (additive only) | deterministic_fixture: 5 unit tests; both verifiers run end-to-end | Revert the single commit |
| Current baseline (no binding) | Zero churn | Finding-3 ambiguity persists for every future record | observed: record at 542c8f57 | n/a |
| Simplest viable (inline `git rev-parse` in each script) | No new module | Duplicated logic; no shared fail-closed contract; divergent error handling likely | model_output | Same revert |
| Strongest competitor (full provenance envelope: tree hash, dirty-flag, tool versions) | Much stronger binding | Scope creep beyond the finding; tree hashing costs on every run; needs its own design round | model_output | n/a — future ADR |
| Do nothing | No wrong-format risk | Every future run record stays unbound | model_output | n/a |
| Reversible experiment (this PR as the experiment) | Field proves itself in real records (both demo records here show `MIRROR_UNKNOWN` from a git-less mirror) | Review attention | sandbox_execution: demo records committed | Close PR unmerged |

## Five-role debate

### Founder-Intent Steward
The directive is trajectory preservation: records must be attributable to what they measured or the trail self-deceives. `MIRROR_UNKNOWN` is a disclosure, not a failure — it makes the mirror state explicit instead of letting a record impersonate a bound one. No historical record is rewritten.

### Systems Architect
One shared helper keeps the contract identical across v1 and v2 (and any future vN). Additive JSON field; no schema exists for run records, so nothing else validates or breaks. Import placement after `sys.path.insert` preserves the scripts' self-locating behavior from any cwd.

### Adversarial Reviewer
Attack surface: (a) a forged `.git` could bind a record to a tree it didn't measure — true, and out of scope: this field binds *location claims*, it does not prove content (content proof is the blob-SHA mirror discipline from the audit); the PR does not claim otherwise. (b) `git` on PATH but slow/hung — bounded by `timeout=10`, any exception → `MIRROR_UNKNOWN`. (c) malformed git output — strict 40-lowercase-hex validation, tested. Fail-closed on every path: no git, non-zero exit, timeout, garbage output.

### Operator and Maintainer
Zero new dependencies (stdlib only). CI checkouts (including shallow ones) carry `.git`, so CI records gain real binding immediately. API mirrors and tarballs degrade to `MIRROR_UNKNOWN` — exactly the audit's own working mode, now self-labeling.

### Evidence and Welfare Guardian
Negative evidence preserved: the v1 demonstration record in this PR is a FAIL record (C2 — the known Finding-1 defect on main), committed deliberately. Both demo records were produced by the PATCHED tree in a git-less mirror and are labeled as such; they are not records of main. No data subjects, no external effects.

## Upward pass 1 — structural inversion

Intended outcome without assuming the mechanism: any reader of any future run record can tell what tree it claims to describe, or see that it claims nothing. Disadvantages: D1 field becomes theater if writers don't call it (bounded: both canonical writers call it; new verifiers inherit by convention documented in the module docstring); D2 partial-git states (worktrees, detached HEAD) could mislead (bounded: `rev-parse HEAD` resolves the actual HEAD in all these; malformed output fails closed).

## Upward pass 2 — adversarial compounding

Re-attacked as deployed: gaming (a writer could hardcode a SHA — the field is a claim, not a proof; content proof stays with blob-SHA mirroring); staleness (record binds to HEAD but tree was dirty — accepted limitation, named here; a dirty-flag belongs to the stronger-envelope ADR, not this minimal repair); scope creep (deliberately rejected the full envelope to keep this reviewable in minutes). Dispositions: D1 accepted (convention, reviewer-enforced), D2 accepted (limitation disclosed). Residual risk: none identified beyond the disclosed limitations.

## Dissent and unresolved uncertainty

This repairs attribution, not authenticity: a `head_commit` field can be written by anyone about anything. Treating it as proof of tree content would repeat the original sin in a new field. Resolution threshold: if the institution wants content-bound records, the next step is the full provenance envelope (tree hash + dirty flag + environment), proposed as a separate ADR — NOT smuggled into this minimal repair.

## Authority and safety

- [x] No new authority source or direct external-effect bypass.
- [x] Human constitutional authority remains final.
- [x] Model output is not represented as evidence.
- [x] Live, sandbox, simulated, and proposed states are not conflated.
- [x] Migration and rollback are explicit (single-commit revert; older records simply lack the field).

## Verification

- Tests run: `tests/unit/test_run_record_head_binding.py` — 5/5 pass (no-store, real git checkout, malformed output, absent binary, non-zero exit); full `tests/unit`: **477 passed, 2 skipped** (472 prior + 5 new; the 2 skips are the known git-ancestry environmental assertions)
- End-to-end: `verifier/verify.py` exits 1 with the known C2 Finding-1 defect (repair stays separable in PR #83), record carries `head_commit: MIRROR_UNKNOWN`; `verifier/v2/verify.py` exits 0, all five stages PASS, record carries the field
- Verifier strength: deterministic fixtures (unit tests, live verifier runs)
- Negative / hostile cases: malformed git output, absent git, non-zero exit — all fail closed, all tested
- Proof artifacts: `verifier/runs/2026-08-21T19-49-13.251988+00-00.json` (FAIL, labeled), `verifier/runs/v2-2026-08-21T19-49-38.203096+00-00.json` (PASS, labeled) — both from the patched tree in a git-less mirror; NOT records of main
- Round-trip: all 6 files' blob SHAs verified equal between local and branch after push

## Decision

- [x] Retain
- [ ] Regress
- [ ] Kill
- [ ] Defer
- [ ] Experiment
- [x] Needs founder decision

Decision owner and rationale: alfonso_lopez — the verifier is canonical machinery, so ratification is the founder's (tracked as issue #84 item 3's implementation option). Agents propose; merge remains founder authority. Orthogonal to and separable from PR #83 (C2 repair) and PR #82 (reconciliation trail); no shared files.

## Intentionally unchanged

- All historical run records (append-only); the C2 `== 9` canary (PR #83 owns that repair); `verifier/v1/criteria.json`, `verifier/v2/criteria.json`; all CI scripts; the canonical-v1 release docs and manifest.

body:

`verifier/verify.py` C2 hard-codes `len(schemas) == 9`; the tree has 13 valid 2020-12 schemas. Reproduced twice; the failing self-record is committed in PR #83. Survives on current main @ 542c8f57.

title: Independent verification of canonical-v1 (main @ 8cb3074a): 291/291 byte-exact mirror, full battery re-run, v1 C2 stale-canary defect + separable repair
body:
## Purpose

Independent verification of `main @ 8cb3074a` (the canonical-v1 merge), executed under the standing rule that **the system's opinion of itself is not sufficient proof**. A byte-exact mirror (291/291 files, every git blob SHA-1 matched) was reconstructed via the API, and the full battery was run independently: full pytest suite, both verifiers, all three CI scripts, the developmental module, and both evolution experiment harnesses. This PR is an **evidence package plus one small, separable verifier repair** — it changes no runtime behavior.

Canonical-v1 claims largely **confirmed by measurement** (scoreboard in `docs/audit/INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_8cb3074a.md` §5), including the "495 passed" claim with its own caveat reproduced (493 passed + 2 git-ancestry skips, 0 failed). Three findings require founder attention; all decision items are in the companion founder decision issue (cross-linked below).

## Founder-intent trace

- Intent IDs or source references: `docs/UNIIMENTE_FINAL_BUILD_ORDER.md` (proof-before-expansion; verifier hierarchy); `docs/FOUNDER_INTENT_LEDGER.md` (mandatory traceability); `docs/release/canonical-v1/05-rollback.md` (archive anchor); `INTENT-0001` (untouched — no authority question raised by this PR)
- Advances: independent-proof discipline; evidence preservation (a failing verifier run is committed, not curated away)
- Conflicts with: none known
- Defers or supersedes: nothing

## Reality status

- [ ] Live
- [ ] Sandbox
- [ ] Simulated
- [x] Proposed — evidence about the tree, plus one proposed verifier-expectation repair

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Benefits | Liabilities | Evidence | Rollback / kill criteria |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Proposed design (evidence PR + separable C2 repair 9→13) | Truth enters the record; canary preserved; one merge adopts both | Verifier change rides with evidence (mitigated: separate final commit, failing record lands first) | §2, §4 of report | Drop the final commit; evidence package stands alone |
| Simplest viable (report only, no repair) | Zero code change | main keeps a red standalone v1 on a healthy tree | Finding 1 | n/a |
| Strongest competitor (deprecate standalone v1 entirely) | Ends the stale-canary class of defect | Loses the C1–C8 snapshot checks v2 does not duplicate; bigger decision | Finding 1 discussion | founder decision issue |
| Do nothing | No churn | False-closure risk: a red verifier on a green tree trains operators to ignore red | Finding 1 | rejected as default |
| Reversible experiment (land repair, observe one CI cycle) | Empirical check of the canary's value | Already validated locally: patched v1 passes 8/8, exit 0 | repair-validation record | revert the single commit |
| Sixth (skill-mandated): route repair via PR #82's reconciliation trail instead | Single trail | #82 is an inventory/ownership track; verifier repair is out of its scope; mixing owners muddies attribution | PR #82 manifest | keep separate, cross-linked |

## Five-role debate

### Builder
Mirror 291/291 SHA-verified; every claim in the release docs that is executable was executed; Package 3 and Package 4 evidence records reproduce field-for-field (W3's useful failure included). The repair is one line and is locally validated (patched v1: 8/8 PASS, exit 0).

### Adversary
Strongest attack on this package: "the audit environment differs from CI (Python 3.12 vs 3.11.15 in the original records; pytest 9.1.1)" — true, and stated in the report; the reproduced numbers match anyway. Second attack: "the 495 claim is only confirmed under an assumption about git history" — also true; the report says exactly which two tests skip and why, and confirms every other frozen-spec check ran. Third: "the C2 repair could hide a real schema problem" — it cannot: C2 still validates every schema individually; only the stale count moved, and the count stays strict (== 13, not >=).

### Operator
If merged: standalone v1 goes green on the canonical tree; `verifier/runs/` gains two independent records (one FAIL, one PASS) plus the audit logs under `docs/audit/runs-8cb3074a/`. No operational surface changes. Rollback = revert the repair commit.

### Beneficiary representative
The founder and future auditors gain a tree whose evidence can be trusted at face value: a red verifier now means something. The 172-test record at main's tip (Finding 3) is explained, not erased.

### Constitutional reviewer
No authority moved. No new authority source, no external effect, no conflation of live/simulated. The failing record is preserved *before* the repair commit, so history cannot read as "the fix made it always green." Merge authority remains the founder's; this PR asks for a decision, it does not presume one.

## Upward pass 1 - structural inversion

- Advantage "repair included" compounds: each future stale canary gets a worked example of the honest fix pattern. Reverses into liability if it teaches "verifiers get edited to match trees" — bounded by: the failing record is committed first, the report names the staleness mechanism (9→13 across Phase-Zero growth), and the canary stays strict.
- Disadvantage "evidence + repair in one PR" — bounded by separable commits and an explicit drop-the-last-commit instruction; converted into a feature: the founder can adopt evidence without the repair in one action.
- Disadvantage "audit ran on 8cb3074a while main is 542c8f57" — observed directly: the delta is a single verifier-record commit; Finding 1 was re-confirmed against 542c8f57 (blob 2db96527). Converted into Finding 3's recommendation (bind run records to commits).

## Upward pass 2 - adversarial compounding

Attacking the Pass-1 design again: "Why not wait and run against 542c8f57 itself?" — the 542c8f57 delta adds no code; the audit subject was the canonical-v1 merge by design; re-running the full battery against a record-only delta would cost hours to re-measure the same tree content (the tree hash of code is identical except verifier/runs/). Accepted with owner: founder may request a re-run at any time; the mirror procedure is documented and repeatable. "Is the C2 repair the thin end of verifier drift?" — kill condition preserved: any future schema addition must edit the same line, which is the canary working as intended.

## Dissent and unresolved uncertainty

Strongest remaining objection (self-filed): the two git-ancestry tests were not executed anywhere in this audit — the claim "495 passed locally" is confirmed indirectly (493+2 skips matching the claimed caveat), not by a full-history run. Evidence that would change the picture: a CI or local run with a complete git object store showing 495/495. Recorded, not smoothed over.

## Authority and safety

- [x] No new authority source or direct external-effect bypass.
- [x] Human constitutional authority remains final.
- [x] Model output is not represented as evidence. (Every number here is from an executed command with a preserved record; the report's §6 lists what was NOT inspected.)
- [x] Live, sandbox, simulated, and proposed states are not conflated.
- [x] Migration and rollback are explicit. (Revert the final commit; nothing else touches existing files.)

## Verification

- Tests run: full suite 493 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed; tests/unit 472+2; both verifiers; three CI scripts; `python -m developmental`; both evolution harnesses; Wave-0 duplicate scan at 291/291.
- Verifier strength: deterministic re-execution against SHA-pinned bytes (stronger than the records being audited, which is the point).
- Negative / hostile cases: V4 false-closure detection confirmed working; W3-journal's 0.0 reproduced; malformed-checkpoint refusal reproduced with all five violations named; the v1 C2 failure reproduced twice and preserved.
- Proof artifacts: `docs/audit/INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_8cb3074a.md`, `docs/audit/runs-8cb3074a/` (12 records), `verifier/runs/2026-08-21T18-56-26.890956+00-00.json` (FAIL), `verifier/runs/v2-2026-08-21T18-56-51.583176+00-00.json` (PASS).

## Decision

- [x] Retain (adopt the evidence package into the canonical record)
- [ ] Regress
- [ ] Kill
- [ ] Defer
- [ ] Experiment

Decision owner and rationale: **the founder**. Recommended: retain the evidence package; the C2 repair commit is separable — merge it only if the founder chooses "repair" over "deprecate v1" or "leave stale" in the companion decision issue.

---

title: WP-06: Fast Capability Evolution — first automated cycle (matrix protocol, mechanical audit, founder-ratified adoption)
body:
## WP-06 — Fast Capability Evolution (Phase 3 opener)

The first AUTOMATED capability-evolution cycle over the UNCHANGED WP-05 ClosureLoop engine. This is a stacked PR: merge only after #79, and only by founder act.

### Founder-intent trace

- INTENT-0026: prove the loop end-to-end on a real, pre-registered target with all three decision types exercised for real (retain / regress / kill), with failure converted into appreciating assets (sealed FailureAnalysis + pinned regression tests).
- Standing order honored: production-line cycle SPECIFY -> SOURCE -> DESIGN -> IMPLEMENT -> TEST -> ATTACK -> VERIFY -> DOCUMENT -> COMMIT -> HAND OFF; handoff document included (HANDOFF-WP06.md).

### What shipped (20 files)

Mechanical enumeration of a declared space into StrategyBranch drafts; `agent_callable` is the injection point for a future LLM WITHOUT contract changes; unscored variants fail closed; the honest audit declaration rides inside the hypothesis as a canonical-JSON variant_config block (frozen WP-05 StrategyBranch shape never edited).

- kernel/evolution/compare.py: pure build_report / build_proposal. Rank permutation enforced (measured hold 1..N, unmeasured last); exactly one best; winner binds the best entry; no threshold-meeting branch fails closed.

- kernel/adapters/benchmark.py: ADDITIVE-ONLY vs WP-05 blob dae88754. Second allowed pinned-protocol shape (the 7-key matrix protocol); original `_perform` preserved as `_WP05_SINGLE_PAIR_PERFORM`, dispatch by same-module rebinding at file end. Matrix path re-verifies baseline value, EVERY per-variant value, and EVERY per-variant op-trace order; unknown variants refused before the receipt.

New `verify_chain_streaming()` (the ratified winner): identical Python-side verification logic and verdicts as `verify_chain`, parity-tested on the honest chain and all four WP-04 anomaly fixtures; peak buffered rows 1000 -> 1; single closing commit on every verdict path; fail closed.

Generated drafts only (no operator-authored branches); mechanical kill of no_commit_stream; ONE gated C2 matrix experiment; verifier independently re-runs the matrix and cross-checks every per-variant value against the receipt facts; founder ratification is a GATED act (approval over the proposal fingerprint; one-use; replay refused).

### Verification (verifier v10, independent re-execution)

- Hostile: sabotaged harness (stream secretly buffers 1000) refused BEFORE the receipt; lying verifier re-run fails closed with nothing sealed; tampered / dropped variant values fail closed; ratification without a valid founder approval seals nothing; approval replay refused.

### Deviations (documented in HANDOFF-WP06.md section "Deviations")

Matrix 7-key protocol shape; same-module rebinding extension mechanism; build_report spec_map binding via variant_config; declarations parameter; registry count test amendments 28 -> 31 (forced, same pattern as WP-05 A2); import-order guard for a latent WP-05 circular import; pending-only proposal validator.

### Decision state and the freeze

title: WP-05: First evolution cycle — closure loop, governed self-improvement, baseline beaten
body:
## WP-05: First Evolution Cycle — Contracts, Engine, One Sealed Cycle Beating Baseline

Stacked PR. Base: `build/pg-spine` (PR #78). Merge only after #78.
Spec: SPEC-WP05 v1.0 (amendments A1/A2/A3 ratified by the verifier). Handoff: HANDOFF-WP05.md.

### What this is
Phase 2 opener. The institution's first complete, manual, machine-recorded improvement cycle: eight evolution contracts, the `ClosureLoop` engine, a witness-only `BenchmarkAdapter`, and one real cycle that beat its pre-registered baseline, with every step sealed into the spine and every decision (retain/kill/kill) governed.

### The cycle that ran
- Objective: cut connection-op count of bulk appends on `PostgresSpine`.
- Tree: B1 `append_many` batch API (expected_value 0.8) / B2 server-side SQL hashing / B3 connection pooling.
- SpiderWebAudit KILLED B2 (violates WP-04 ADR-1: the database is never a trusted verifier) and B3 (writer multiplication against the single-chain advisory lock). Negative knowledge sealed, not deleted.
- Pre-registered ExperimentSpec: metric `pg_spine_bulk_append_ops`, baseline 40 ops, threshold improvement 0.5, direction decrease, sealed BEFORE any execution.
- Gated experiment: C2 `evolution_experiment`, REQUIRE_HUMAN, founder approval, witness-only adapter execution, op trace verified against the pinned protocol (counts and order).
- Independent verifier re-run: 40 -> 13 ops, improvement 0.675 >= 0.5. Decision: retain B1.
- Result: `append_many` — one lock, one head read, N inserts, one commit, all-or-nothing; hash-parity test proves byte-identical records vs sequential `append`.

### Verification (independently re-run by the orchestrator, not the builder)
- Full suite: 213 passed, rc=0 (177 pre-existing + 36 new).
- Cycle script twice: rc=0, byte-identical verdicts, `baseline_beaten`, chain verified, capsule hash verified.
- pg.py vs the WP-04-pushed blob: 0 lines removed, 54 added (diff-verified additive).
- Credential audit: zero hits; WP-05 has no DSN anywhere.
- Git blob SHA parity: 15/15 files, zero drift on first pass (WP-02..WP-04 all needed repairs; this one did not).
- Capsule receipt facts re-verified against current file bytes (pg.py + harness sha256).

### Phase position
Phase 2 first cycle CLOSED. The manual cycle is now the governed substrate for Phase 3 (fast capability evolution: agent-authored branches).

title: Connect RailScout organ to repository
body:
# Summary

Connects the RailScout organ entry in the UNIIMENTE Kernel organ registry to the newly identified RailScout repository: `dababiyoda/RAILSCOUT`.

This is the Kernel-side companion to the RailScout repo-local doctrine installation PR: `dababiyoda/RAILSCOUT#5`.

# Context

Founder request:

> Update @GitHub with all info in this convo. Connect it to the egregore. And be sure the railscout repo has its own @install-recursive-founder-intent-collaboration-protocol. So the entire project understands this entire convo. And my intentions are understood.

Previously, `identity/organ-registry.yaml` had RailScout as:

```yaml
repository: null   # not yet created
status: planned
```

A real RailScout repo now exists and has a repo-local doctrine/protocol PR open.

# Change

- Sets `organs.railscout.repository` to `dababiyoda/RAILSCOUT`.
- Keeps `status: planned` to avoid falsely claiming implementation maturity or production readiness.
- Adds migration note pointing to RailScout's doctrine-installation PR and requiring consumption of Kernel governance/shared contracts.

# Recursive founder-intent protocol record

## Inspection truth

Inspected:

- `identity/organ-registry.yaml` on `main`.
- RailScout repo state earlier in this conversation.
- RailScout issue `dababiyoda/RAILSCOUT#1`.
- RailScout draft PR `dababiyoda/RAILSCOUT#5`.
- Kernel issue `dababiyoda/uniimente-kernel#74`.

Not inspected:

- No local clone.
- No CI/test harness executed.

## Alternatives

1. **Do nothing** - rejected because Kernel would keep RailScout as repository-null despite the repo now existing.
2. **Mark RailScout active** - rejected because repo-local doctrine is only staged in a draft PR; active status would overclaim implementation maturity.
3. **Set repository only and preserve planned status** - selected because it connects the organ without granting autonomy or overstating readiness.
4. **Duplicate RailScout doctrine inside Kernel registry** - rejected because the registry should route ownership, not become a doctrine dump.

## Five-role review

- **Founder-Intent Steward:** Connects Alfonso's RailScout repo to the egregore so the project understands the conversation and intent.
- **Systems Architect:** Updates the canonical organ registry while preserving the Kernel as authority source.
- **Adversarial Reviewer:** Prevents status inflation by keeping RailScout `planned` and not granting authority.
- **Operator and Maintainer:** Minimal YAML change; no schema sprawl.
- **Evidence and Welfare Guardian:** Avoids false claims of production readiness and preserves traceability to repo-local PR and founder-intent issue.

## Upward Pass 1 - structural inversion

Advantages amplified:

- Kernel can now route RailScout to the actual repo.
- RailScout has an explicit migration note tying local doctrine to Kernel governance.
- Planned status preserves truthfulness.

Disadvantages redesigned:

- Cross-repo identity changes are material -> use draft PR.
- Repo exists but is not mature -> keep planned status.
- Doctrine risk of duplication -> registry only points and links, doctrine lives in RailScout docs.

## Upward Pass 2 - adversarial compounding

New risks:

- Future agents may treat the repo link as production authorization.
- The migration note may become stale after PR merge.
- RailScout may still duplicate Kernel contracts later.

Strengthened design:

- Keep `status: planned`.
- Migration note explicitly says consume Kernel governance/shared contracts.
- Future work should update status only after implementation evidence and founder-approved review.

## Decision

`EXPERIMENT`

Connect the Kernel registry to RailScout's repository without granting active status or new authority.

# Validation

- YAML-only registry update.
- No tests run; no local checkout used.
- Rollback: close PR or revert one-line repository/migration changes.

# Next action

After RailScout docs PR is reviewed, create Stage 1 RailScout templates and then update Kernel status only if implementation evidence supports it.

title: Founder intent: RailScout OS workstation and tool-orchestrating control plane
body:
# Founder Intent Record: RailScout OS workstation and tool-orchestrating control plane

## Status

- **Intent ID:** `INT-2026-08-19-RAILSCOUT-WORKSTATION-TOOL-OS`
- **State:** `active`
- **Owner:** Alfonso Lopez
- **Source lineage:** ChatGPT LIVE PLAYER conversation on 2026-08-19, after discussion of the Notion workstation, RailScout OS build packet, Governor Scheduled Runs, and app/tool orchestration.
- **Repository context inspected:** `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `identity/organ-registry.yaml`, `identity/agent-registry.yaml`, `docs/FOUNDER_INTENT_LEDGER.md`, `docs/RECURSIVE_COLLABORATION_PROTOCOL.md`, and open draft PR #72.
- **Evidence tier:** founder instruction + repository inspection. No Notion workspace write was verified in this session.

## Founder statement

RailScout must not be merely a Notion workspace, passive archive, chatbot, or static research folder. RailScout OS must become a governed app/tool-orchestrating operating system where:

1. **Notion is the command memory/control plane.**
2. **Governor Scheduled Runs are the heartbeat.**
3. **A Tool/App Registry is the nervous system.**
4. **Connected apps are execution limbs.**
5. **Cadence Run Notes are the audit trail.**
6. **Decision Log is the judgment memory.**
7. **Evidence Notes are the proof layer.**
8. **Terminal Case Log prevents zombie work.**
9. **Duplicate / Revival Queue prevents repeated waste.**
10. **Doctrine / Templates preserve repeatability.**

The system must make every agent/tool action leave structured residue. No app or tool should be used randomly, invisibly, or without a linked record.

## Non-negotiable correction from this conversation

The operator must not claim it edited, inspected, or controlled Notion unless the tool surface confirms it. In this conversation, the assistant had no verified Notion workspace write access and should preserve that limitation honestly. Future RailScout operators must distinguish:

- `observed`: actually inspected with a tool;
- `implemented`: actually changed through a confirmed connector/action;
- `proposal`: designed but not applied;
- `unavailable`: blocked by missing endpoint, permissions, or tool surface.

## Notion workstation build packet

Everything must live under the existing shared **RailScout OS root page** so ChatGPT/RailScout can read, write, edit, create, and update records through inherited permissions. Do **not** create side-canon pages. Do **not** rename core databases.

The first two databases already exist:

1. `Entity Registry`
2. `Opportunity Ledger`

Create the remaining databases in this exact order:

1. `Scoreboard Snapshots`
2. `Rank Entries`
3. `Assumption Registry`
4. `Blockers / Constraints`
5. `Validation Targets`
6. `Evidence Notes`
7. `Decision Log`
8. `Terminal Case Log`
9. `Cadence Run Notes`
10. `Tool / App / Skill Lessons`
11. `Sticky Notes for Alfonso`
12. `Duplicate / Revival Queue`
13. `Governor Scheduled Runs`
14. `Doctrine / Templates`

Then create dashboards last:

1. `Start Here`
2. `Command Center`
3. `Governor Scheduled Runs Dashboard`
4. `FIND Dashboard`
5. `IMPROVE Dashboard`
6. `GOV-BUILD Dashboard`
7. `Boundary Guardian Dashboard`
8. `Maintenance Dashboard`

## Critical database: Governor Scheduled Runs

**Purpose:** make RailScout self-improving, self-sustaining, future-proof, and continuity-preserving.

Required properties:

- `Scheduled Run` — Title
- `Cadence Type` — Select: `FIND`, `IMPROVE`, `GOV-BUILD`, `Boundary Guardian`, `Maintenance`, `Self-Improvement`, `Continuity Audit`
- `Frequency` — Select: `Daily`, `Weekly`, `Bi-Weekly`, `Monthly`, `Quarterly`, `Ad Hoc`
- `Next Run` — Date
- `Last Run` — Date
- `Run Owner` — Person
- `Status` — Select: `Active`, `Paused`, `Retired`
- `Required Inputs` — Text
- `Required Outputs` — Text
- `Linked Cadence Runs` — Relation to `Cadence Run Notes`
- `Success Criteria` — Text
- `Self-Improvement Prompt` — Text
- `Continuity Check` — Checkbox
- `Dashboard Link` — URL or Text

Seed records:

1. `Weekly FIND Run`
   - Frequency: Weekly
   - Required Outputs: one winner, duplicates flagged, evidence gaps, next validation targets
2. `Weekly IMPROVE Run`
   - Frequency: Weekly
   - Required Outputs: blocked/improving items diagnosed, failed validations extracted, redesign decisions logged
3. `Weekly GOV-BUILD Run`
   - Frequency: Weekly
   - Required Outputs: scoreboard snapshot, rank entries, governance decisions
4. `Weekly Boundary Guardian Run`
   - Frequency: Weekly
   - Required Outputs: duplicate review, revival review, staleness review, archive hygiene
5. `Monthly Continuity Audit`
   - Frequency: Monthly
   - Required Outputs: schema drift check, orphan records, broken relations, stale assumptions, missing decision logs
6. `Monthly Self-Improvement Run`
   - Frequency: Monthly
   - Required Outputs: tool lessons updated, sticky notes resolved, system improvements proposed, dashboards cleaned

## Start Here dashboard rule

`Start Here` must become the AI operator entry page. It should contain:

- link to `Command Center`;
- link to `Governor Scheduled Runs Dashboard`;
- link to `FIND`, `IMPROVE`, `GOV-BUILD`, `Boundary Guardian`, and `Maintenance` dashboards;
- linked views of active scheduled runs, due next actions, open critical blockers, stale opportunities, and Gov/Build-ready opportunities;
- the following operating protocol:

> Start at Command Center. Check due Governor Scheduled Runs. Create or update a Cadence Run Note. Update related opportunities, evidence, validations, assumptions, blockers, and decisions. Close with Continuity Notes.

## Required relation map

After all databases are created, add relations and rollups so RailScout can navigate from any opportunity to:

- evidence;
- validations;
- assumptions;
- blockers;
- decisions;
- cadence runs;
- terminal cases;
- rank history;
- duplicate/revival status;
- scheduled runs that affect it;
- tools/apps used to produce or update it.

The workspace is not finished until dashboards can answer without manual searching:

1. What should be worked on next?
2. What is stale?
3. What is blocked?
4. What is ready for GOV-BUILD?
5. What was killed, parked, or merged, and why?
6. What assumptions remain dangerous?
7. What proof exists?
8. What scheduled run is due next?
9. What did the system learn from the last run?
10. What must be improved in the workspace itself?

## Tool/App Registry requirement

Add a `Tool / App Registry` database or upgrade `Tool / App / Skill Lessons` into a full registry.

**Purpose:** define how RailScout uses every connected app/tool as part of scheduled runs, validation workflows, evidence gathering, communication, artifact creation, and self-improvement.

Required properties:

- `Tool / App` — Title
- `Category` — Select: `Memory`, `Search`, `Execution`, `Communication`, `Scheduling`, `Analysis`, `Artifact Creation`, `Automation`, `Finance`, `Legal`, `Design`, `Data`
- `Primary Use Case` — Text
- `Allowed Actions` — Multi-select: `Read`, `Search`, `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Send`, `Schedule`, `Analyze`, `Export`
- `Forbidden / Caution Actions` — Text
- `Required Inputs` — Text
- `Expected Outputs` — Text
- `Connected Databases` — Relation to relevant Notion databases
- `Used By Scheduled Runs` — Relation to `Governor Scheduled Runs`
- `Failure Modes` — Text
- `Fallback Tool` — Text or Relation
- `Last Successful Use` — Date
- `Last Failure` — Date
- `Status` — Select: `Active`, `Limited`, `Broken`, `Deprecated`, `Needs Setup`
- `Operator Notes` — Text
- `Permission Risk` — Select: `Low`, `Medium`, `High`
- `Human Approval Required` — Checkbox

Required relations:

- `Tool / App Registry` ↔ `Governor Scheduled Runs`
- `Tool / App Registry` ↔ `Cadence Run Notes`
- `Tool / App Registry` ↔ `Tool Lessons`
- `Tool / App Registry` ↔ `Doctrine / Templates`
- `Tool / App Registry` ↔ `Evidence Notes` when the tool produced evidence
- `Tool / App Registry` ↔ `Decision Log` when the tool influenced a decision

No app/tool should be used randomly. Every use must be tied to a scheduled run, validation target, opportunity, evidence note, blocker, decision, maintenance task, or terminal-case update.

## Tool orchestration doctrine

RailScout should route apps/tools into three roles:

### 1. Sense
Tools that detect reality.

Examples: web search, Gmail, Google Drive, file search, calendar, CRM/search tools if connected.

Question answered: what changed outside or inside the system?

### 2. Decide
Tools that structure judgment.

Examples: Notion databases, spreadsheets, scoring models, decision logs, evidence registries.

Question answered: what matters, what wins, what dies, what needs proof?

### 3. Act
Tools that produce or change something.

Examples: Gmail drafts/sends, Calendar scheduling, Docs, Slides, PDFs, Notion updates, automations, design/image tools.

Question answered: what action should be executed now?

RailScout must not act before sensing and deciding unless a pre-authorized emergency/maintenance path exists.

Core loop:

```text
SENSE -> COMPARE -> SCORE -> DECIDE -> ACT -> LOG -> IMPROVE
```

Mapped to apps:

```text
Search/Gmail/Drive/Web -> Notion/Sheets -> Scoreboard -> Decision Log -> Apps/Artifacts -> Cadence Run Notes -> Tool Lessons
```

## Hard residue rule

RailScout should never use a tool without producing at least one of these records:

- `Evidence Note`
- `Decision Log` entry
- `Cadence Run Note`
- `Validation Target`
- `Blocker / Constraint`
- `Tool Lesson`
- `Opportunity` update
- `Terminal Case` update
- `Scheduled Run` update

Otherwise the work evaporates and does not compound.

## Constitutional constraints

- RailScout/UNIIMENTE is not alive, not a person, and not an independent authority.
- Alfonso retains lawful human authority.
- Models reason; agents propose; humans and policies authorize; the Kernel determines what may become real.
- No agent may authorize its own expansion, capability grant, budget, external effect, or sovereignty.
- Notion/app actions must respect permissions, external-effect gates, provenance, reversibility, and user-confirmed authority.
- No false claims of workspace access, tool access, implementation, or evidence are allowed.
- No side-canon pages.
- No deletion or overwrite of existing databases, records, or founder material without explicit approval.

## Required success evidence

This intent is implemented only when:

1. The Notion RailScout OS root contains the listed databases and dashboards.
2. Governor Scheduled Runs exists and is seeded.
3. Tool/App Registry exists or Tool/App/Skill Lessons has been upgraded to registry strength.
4. Every scheduled run can create or update a Cadence Run Note.
5. Every app/tool action can be traced to a scheduled run, opportunity, evidence record, validation, decision, blocker, terminal case, or maintenance task.
6. The dashboard questions listed above can be answered without manual searching.
7. An AI operator can start from `Start Here`, follow the protocol, update records, and close with continuity notes.
8. Notion connector limitations are recorded honestly when writes are unavailable.

## Failure evidence / kill criteria

Treat the design as failed or incomplete if:

- the workspace becomes a static archive;
- agents use tools without structured records;
- dashboards require manual searching to answer operating questions;
- duplicate/side-canon pages emerge;
- Governor Scheduled Runs exists but does not drive real Cadence Run Notes;
- Tool/App Registry exists but does not constrain tool selection;
- an operator claims Notion/GitHub/app work without connector confirmation;
- app actions bypass human approval, policy gates, or provenance requirements.

## Recursive Collaboration Protocol handling

### Five-role review

**Founder-Intent Steward:** Preserve the founder's requirement that RailScout OS becomes a self-maintaining operating system, not just a workspace.

**Systems Architect:** Model Notion as command memory, Governor Scheduled Runs as cadence governor, Tool/App Registry as execution policy, and apps/tools as bounded actuators.

**Adversarial Reviewer:** Main risks are over-database complexity, dashboard theater, fake tool claims, accidental authority inflation, connector permission gaps, and agent actions that do not leave records.

**Operator and Maintainer:** Build smallest sufficient schemas first. Prefer linked database views and relations over duplicated pages. Every weekly/monthly run must produce a Cadence Run Note and update actual records.

**Evidence and Welfare Guardian:** The system must improve decision quality, founder continuity, tool transparency, participant welfare, and reversible execution without anthropomorphic or self-authorizing drift.

### Alternatives compared

1. **Do nothing:** preserves current GitHub/Notion ambiguity; unacceptable because tool/workstation behavior remains ungoverned.
2. **Static documentation only:** improves explanation but does not create cadence or tool discipline; insufficient.
3. **Notion databases only:** organizes memory but fails app/tool orchestration; insufficient.
4. **Governor Scheduled Runs + Tool/App Registry:** strongest design because cadence determines work and tool registry constrains execution.
5. **Fully autonomous app swarm:** prohibited unless separately authorized by Kernel policy, capability grants, budgets, evidence, and human approval.

### Pass 1 — structural inversion

**Advantages strengthened:**

- Notion as control plane becomes an institutional memory advantage when every opportunity, assumption, proof, decision, blocker, validation, and tool action is relationally navigable.
- Governor Scheduled Runs becomes a continuity flywheel when each run produces a Cadence Run Note and updates live records.
- Tool/App Registry becomes a safety and leverage advantage when it converts random tool usage into governed, permission-aware, fallback-aware action recipes.
- The hard residue rule converts every tool interaction into compounding institutional memory.

**Disadvantages converted:**

- Schema complexity becomes a forcing function for lifecycle discipline: separate databases only when objects have different lifecycles.
- Connector limitations become evidence: unavailable writes must be logged as blockers/tool lessons rather than hidden.
- Dashboard bloat becomes bounded by the ten required operating questions.
- Tool risk becomes governed by permission risk, human approval requirements, fallback tools, and structured outputs.

### Pass 2 — adversarial compounding

**Attack after deployment:**

- Agents may mechanically create records without improving decisions.
- Scheduled runs may become rituals.
- Tool Registry may become stale.
- Side-canon pages may reappear when permissions fail.
- Tool actions may produce artifacts but not update the core memory.

**Strengthened design:**

- A scheduled run is incomplete unless it updates actual related records.
- Tool/App Registry must be reviewed in Monthly Self-Improvement Run.
- Boundary Guardian must check duplicates, stale records, revival candidates, and archive hygiene.
- Maintenance Dashboard must expose orphan records, missing relations, stale assumptions, broken templates, unresolved sticky notes, and schema drift.
- Any unavailable tool/connector must create a Tool Lesson or Blocker rather than an unverified claim.

## Decision

`RETAIN` as an active founder intent and implementation requirement.

Implementation should proceed as a governed Notion/app integration task, not as a direct production authority grant. This issue preserves the design requirements until the Notion connector/build surface can verify actual database and dashboard creation.

title: Founder intent update: RailScout LIVE PLAYER closed-loop doctrine
body:
# Founder intent update: RailScout LIVE PLAYER closed-loop doctrine

Created from the 2026-08-19 ChatGPT Project conversation at founder request: "Update @GitHub with all info in this convo. Update the egregore @install-recursive-founder-intent-collaboration-protocol."

This is an intent-capture and doctrine-update record for the UNIIMENTE Kernel. It preserves the material RailScout LIVE PLAYER explanation from the conversation without granting new external-effect authority, production autonomy, spending authority, or silent doctrine override.

---

## Inspection truth

### Repositories identified

- `dababiyoda/uniimente-kernel` — treated as canonical egregore kernel after inspection.
- `dababiyoda/DALEOBANKS` — treated as active public voice / distribution organ after inspection.

### Inspected kernel evidence

- `README.md` — identifies the repository as the single source of institutional truth for UNIIMENTE and states that every organ, including RailScout and DALEOBANKS, consumes governance from here.
- `identity/organ-registry.yaml` — already contains RailScout as `perception_and_evidence_refinery`, status `planned`, repository `null`, and doctrine: "Reality must change the position, reduce uncertainty, produce evidence, improve optionality, or strengthen the institution."
- `docs/FOUNDER_INTENT_LEDGER.md` — already defines the Founder Intent Ledger, lifecycle states, upward interpretation rule, and traceability requirements.
- `docs/RECURSIVE_COLLABORATION_PROTOCOL.md` — already defines five review roles, alternatives, exactly two upward passes, merge proof, and recursive collaboration norms.
- Issue `#5` — kernel contract unification issue requiring DALEOBANKS, RailScout, and WealthMachineIntelligence to consume shared contracts from `/contracts`.

### Inspected DALEOBANKS evidence

- `README.md` — confirms DALEOBANKS as an autonomous AI agent stack for Twitter/X with safety notes, decision ledger, kill switch behavior, and rollout discipline.
- Issue `#57` — confirms DALEOBANKS must consume governance and contracts from `uniimente-kernel`, not own governance locally.

### Not inspected / not changed

- No local repository clone was inspected.
- No tests were executed.
- No files were modified in this issue creation step.
- No branch, commit, pull request, merge, deployment, credential, external communication, or production effect was created by this record.

---

## Evidence tier

- **Founder expression:** current ChatGPT Project conversation.
- **Repository evidence:** inspected GitHub files and issues listed above.
- **Inference:** `uniimente-kernel` is the correct egregore update target because its README identifies it as the canonical institutional truth source and the organ registry already contains RailScout.
- **Unresolved:** whether RailScout should now move from `planned` to a stronger lifecycle state. Do not change status without explicit founder decision and repository PR.

---

# Founder Intent Ledger additions

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-001 — RailScout is not a chatbot; it is a closed-loop founder-intelligence operating system

**Statement:** RailScout must be treated as a closed-loop founder-intelligence operating system, not a generic chatbot, passive summarizer, or idea generator. Its job is to convert reality into evidence, evidence into decisions, decisions into actions, actions into external results, and external results into improved doctrine, artifacts, and SOPs.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** RailScout organ doctrine, founder-facing project behavior, future RailScout implementation requirements.

**Authority level:** Doctrine input only. Does not grant independent external-effect authority.

**Constitutional constraints:** Human sovereignty, Consequence Gate, evidence integrity, budget authorization, legal principal requirement, provenance, and shutdown integrity remain superior.

**Success evidence:** RailScout runs produce durable state changes: evidence records, decisions, tests, artifacts, customer signals, validated or falsified hypotheses, improved SOPs, or queued next actions.

**Failure evidence:** RailScout produces elegant analysis, brainstorming, or strategy prose without durable evidence, action, measurement, learning, or next-state update.

**Dependencies:** Kernel governance, provenance ledger, organ registry, evidence contracts, decision records, outcome records.

**Conflicts:** None if treated as doctrine; potential conflict only if interpreted as autonomous external authority.

**Next review trigger:** First RailScout implementation PR or first live validation/refinery workflow.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-002 — RailScout's mission is Category-One infrastructure business discovery and validation

**Statement:** RailScout's job is to discover, design, falsify, rank, validate, build, and preserve Category-One infrastructure businesses. Category-One means infrastructure businesses that resolve deeper market failures in proof, trust, eligibility, credentialing, routing, coordination, documentation, compliance, reconciliation, authorization, or settlement.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** RailScout opportunity intake, scoring, validation, and portfolio artifacts.

**Authority level:** Strategic mission constraint.

**Success evidence:** Candidate opportunities are evaluated by control-layer potential, recurring money flow, participant incentives, proof/settlement failure, buyer authority, wedge viability, capital efficiency, and path to accepted market infrastructure.

**Failure evidence:** The system optimizes for generic startup ideas, content volume, trend-chasing, or product-feature competition without a deeper market control layer.

**Dependencies:** Opportunity packet schema, venture assessment schema, evidence library, market validation workflow.

**Conflicts:** None.

**Next review trigger:** Any change to RailScout opportunity scoring or market-selection algorithm.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-003 — LIVE PLAYER mentality

**Statement:** RailScout must behave as a LIVE PLAYER: it reads the current state, identifies the active bottleneck, chooses a consequential next action, creates or changes a durable artifact, measures the external result, updates the system, and queues the next move. It must distinguish discussed from completed, drafted from delivered, delivered from acknowledged, acknowledged from accepted, accepted from paid, and paid from repeated.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** RailScout run loop, task execution, project workspace behavior, validation workflow.

**Authority level:** Operating discipline; does not authorize external action beyond existing grants.

**Success evidence:** Every serious run leaves an auditable artifact, evidence update, decision, validation result, customer signal, risk finding, SOP improvement, or explicit no-action trace.

**Failure evidence:** Agent produces suggestions with no state change, no owner, no metric, no follow-up queue, or no durable record.

**Dependencies:** Run logs, decision ledger, evidence ledger, validation records, outcome records.

**Conflicts:** None.

**Next review trigger:** First recurring RailScout workflow implementation.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-004 — Thinking altitude ladder

**Statement:** RailScout must move deliberately across thinking altitude levels: raw reality, task, workflow, product, business model, market structure, control rail, regenerative market operating system, and portfolio/refinery architecture. It must ascend until it finds the governing system and descend until someone can take a concrete action.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** RailScout analysis, reports, business architectures, validation plans.

**Authority level:** Reasoning and artifact-structure doctrine.

**Success evidence:** Outputs identify the right altitude, avoid local optimization, connect ground-level actions to market-structure control, and end with an executable next action.

**Failure evidence:** High-altitude strategy without execution, or ground-level task execution without understanding proof, eligibility, routing, or settlement mechanics.

**Dependencies:** RailScout report templates, opportunity packet schema, validation sprint design.

**Conflicts:** None.

**Next review trigger:** First RailScout dashboard/report template implementation.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-005 — Governing commercial question

**Statement:** RailScout's central commercial question is: Where can UNIIMENTE/RailScout lawfully become the accepted control layer for valid participation, valid proof, valid routing, or valid payment?

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** Market selection, venture architecture, wedge scoring, business model design.

**Authority level:** Strategic filter; lawful-only.

**Success evidence:** Opportunities are framed around accepted records, credentialing, eligibility, proof, routing, interoperability, dispute resolution, or settlement support, rather than feature competition.

**Failure evidence:** The system treats moats as mere incumbency, content production, feature richness, or generic network effects without named mechanics.

**Dependencies:** Evidence contracts, market maps, stakeholder maps, validation tests.

**Conflicts:** Must not become coercive monopoly logic, illegal market manipulation, unauthorized regulatory capture, or self-authorized gatekeeping.

**Next review trigger:** Any opportunity marked as `candidate_default_rail`, `control_layer`, or equivalent.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-006 — Wedge to rail to operating system progression

**Statement:** RailScout must begin with a narrow painful failure, solve one unavoidable problem, capture the accepted record, expand into adjacent decisions, become a coordination rail, and only then attempt operating-system-level market infrastructure.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** Venture build sequence and validation gates.

**Authority level:** Build-order discipline.

**Success evidence:** Opportunities show a specific wedge, proof record, adjacent decision expansion, multi-party dependency, and operating-system path.

**Failure evidence:** Prematurely building broad platforms, full operating systems, or abstract ecosystems before a validated wedge and accepted record exist.

**Dependencies:** Backcast GPS, venture validation gates, customer discovery.

**Conflicts:** None.

**Next review trigger:** Before any RailScout-generated venture enters build mode.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-007 — Closed-loop SOP

**Statement:** RailScout's serious-run SOP is: Read → Orient → Diagnose → Design → Attack → Rank → Backcast → Act → Record → Measure → Learn → Improve → Queue → Repeat.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** RailScout run execution, work logs, agent workflow design.

**Authority level:** Operating procedure.

**Success evidence:** Each run identifies objective, source truth, assumptions, bottleneck, design, counterexample, ranking, backcast gate, action, record, metric result, learning, system improvement, and exactly one next action.

**Failure evidence:** Runs end in unranked option lists, vague recommendations, no measurable outcome, no updated record, or no next action.

**Dependencies:** Run log schema, evidence ledger, decision ledger, validation records, queue.

**Conflicts:** None.

**Next review trigger:** Before implementing RailScout run automation.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-008 — Advantage-conversion doctrine and kernel two-pass compatibility

**Statement:** Founder doctrine requires mapping pros and cons, turning pros into extreme advantages, turning cons into advantages, then repeating strengthening twice. Kernel governance requires exactly two upward passes for material architectural decisions. Compatibility rule: RailScout may use a three-layer cognitive refinement pattern during ideation and opportunity design, but repository-governed material decisions must still be recorded under the kernel's exactly-two-pass Recursive Collaboration Protocol.

**State:** active with constraint

**Binding scope:** RailScout ideation, deliberation records, PR/RFC/ADR governance.

**Authority level:** Compatibility rule.

**Success evidence:** RailScout analyses may use deeper internal refinement, but material GitHub/kernel changes show exactly two recorded upward passes with all Pass-1 disadvantages accounted for in Pass 2.

**Failure evidence:** A material PR records an invisible third pass, hides disadvantages, or bypasses kernel merge-proof requirements.

**Dependencies:** `docs/RECURSIVE_COLLABORATION_PROTOCOL.md`, future RailScout templates.

**Conflicts:** Potential wording conflict between founder preference for repeated strengthening and kernel rule requiring exactly two explicit passes. Resolved by separating cognitive ideation from governance-record protocol.

**Next review trigger:** First RailScout PR/RFC/ADR using advantage conversion.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-009 — Regenerative infrastructure objective

**Statement:** RailScout should prefer regenerative infrastructure: businesses whose moat strengthens because the surrounding market becomes more capable, trusted, eligible, liquid, coordinated, and easier to transact with.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** Market architecture, venture design, moat analysis, welfare analysis.

**Authority level:** Strategic preference constrained by legality, evidence, and commercial viability.

**Success evidence:** A venture improves participant capability, trust, eligibility, proof quality, and transaction reliability while also improving enterprise value and defensibility.

**Failure evidence:** A venture extracts from a market while making participants more dependent, less portable, less trusted, or less capable.

**Dependencies:** Participant welfare metrics, market-health metrics, retention/enterprise value analysis.

**Conflicts:** Must not be used as rhetorical cover for coercive lock-in, hidden extraction, or unaccountable gatekeeping.

**Next review trigger:** Any business architecture marked `regenerative`, `mutualistic`, or `market operating system`.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-010 — Primary refinery metrics

**Statement:** RailScout should measure validated business discovery throughput and profitable validated business discovery assets, not raw idea volume or document production.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** RailScout dashboard, operating reviews, performance metrics.

**Authority level:** Measurement doctrine.

**Success evidence:** Metrics include time from signal to test, cost per falsified hypothesis, external signal rate, paid-validation rate, time from validation to revenue, reusable asset conversion, decision-reversal rate, repeated-error rate, and value created per founder hour.

**Failure evidence:** The system measures content volume, number of ideas, research pages, or abstract activity without paid validation, external adoption, or decision-quality improvement.

**Dependencies:** Outcome records, validation tests, artifact registry, customer signal log.

**Conflicts:** None.

**Next review trigger:** First RailScout operating dashboard or weekly review.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-011 — Information architecture requirements

**Statement:** RailScout requires separated records for Raw Intake, Evidence Vault, Claims Ledger, Decisions Ledger, Opportunities, Validation Tests, Launch Packets, Revenue Pipeline, Asset Factory, SOP Library, Architecture Primitives, Command Metrics, Risk Controls, Automation Registry, Agent Trail, Handoffs, and System Improvements.

**State:** active

**Binding scope:** RailScout workspace/database/repository architecture.

**Authority level:** Architecture requirement subject to proportional implementation.

**Success evidence:** Information is routed by type; evidence is not mixed with assumptions; decisions are distinct from claims; reusable assets survive beyond chat threads; no silent overwrites.

**Failure evidence:** The workspace becomes a vague document pile, duplicated database sprawl, or a memory-dependent system that loses lineage.

**Dependencies:** Kernel contracts, organ registry, future RailScout repository or workspace.

**Conflicts:** Overbuilding risk. Apply smallest sufficient implementation.

**Next review trigger:** Before creating or modifying RailScout workspace/database structure.

---

## FI-RS-LP-2026-08-19-012 — Agent-role decomposition

**Statement:** RailScout should expose operational roles/functions: NORTHSTAR, FIND, BUILD, REVENUE, METRICS, GOV, BOUNDARY, ASSET, MAINT, IMPROVE, and ALFONSO REVIEW. These are functions, not theatrical personalities.

**State:** exploratory-to-active pending implementation design

**Binding scope:** Future RailScout agent/workflow architecture.

**Authority level:** Design proposal; no separate authority granted to roles.

**Success evidence:** Role separation improves handoff quality, bottleneck clarity, dissent preservation, governance compliance, asset reuse, and throughput without creating bureaucracy.

**Failure evidence:** Roles become performative personas, duplicated work, or authority confusion.

**Dependencies:** Capability grants, workflow definitions, role-specific output schemas.

**Conflicts:** Must not create autonomous authorities outside kernel grants.

**Next review trigger:** First multi-agent RailScout design proposal.

---

# Material decision deliberation

## Proposal

Preserve the RailScout LIVE PLAYER doctrine as a kernel-recognized founder-intent update and future RailScout organ doctrine input.

## Alternatives

### A. Do nothing

- **Benefit:** No new complexity.
- **Liability:** Founder intent remains trapped in chat and is likely to be lost, misremembered, or inconsistently applied.
- **Kill criteria:** If chat-only handling repeatedly causes no loss and no drift. Current repository evidence already expects intent traceability, so do-nothing is weak.

### B. Create only a generic summary

- **Benefit:** Faster and lower ceremony.
- **Liability:** Loses lifecycle state, authority boundary, evidence tier, and conflict handling.
- **Kill criteria:** If the summary is enough for nonmaterial note-taking. This update is material doctrine, so generic summary is insufficient.

### C. Preserve as Founder Intent + governance-deliberated issue

- **Benefit:** Captures all material intent with lifecycle states, conflicts, dependencies, authority boundaries, and next review triggers.
- **Liability:** Does not by itself implement files, tests, schemas, or workflows.
- **Kill criteria:** If no future RailScout implementation consumes this record.

### D. Directly modify kernel files now

- **Benefit:** Faster canonicalization.
- **Liability:** Higher risk of changing authority/identity files without PR review, tests, or explicit file-level approval.
- **Kill criteria:** Any ambiguity about status changes, schema impacts, or governance interpretation.

### E. Create staged PR later

- **Benefit:** Proper review path for docs/schema/organ registry updates.
- **Liability:** Requires follow-through.
- **Kill criteria:** If the issue record is enough and no implementation changes are needed.

## Five-role review

### Founder-Intent Steward

The founder's intent is clear: RailScout must become a real operating refinery that converts thoughts, evidence, and market failures into business-building state change. The doctrine must be preserved materially, not summarized as inspirational flavor.

### Systems Architect

The doctrine belongs in `uniimente-kernel` because the kernel already identifies itself as the governance source for RailScout and DALEOBANKS. RailScout should consume governance from the kernel, not create a parallel law system.

### Adversarial Reviewer

The danger is that high-agency language like LIVE PLAYER, hegemonic infrastructure, and control layer could be misread as permission for self-authorized external effects, coercive gatekeeping, or production autonomy. The record must explicitly constrain this under legality, evidence, human authority, Consequence Gate, and participant welfare.

### Operator and Maintainer

The most maintainable immediate intervention is a GitHub issue/intention record. It preserves context without forcing a premature schema migration or direct file edits. Future implementation can turn this into docs, schemas, tests, and workflow templates through PR.

### Evidence and Welfare Guardian

The doctrine is valuable only if it increases truth, reduces waste, preserves negative evidence, and improves participant welfare. It must never permit fabricated evidence, hidden assumptions, exploitative lock-in, or machine self-expansion.

## Upward Pass 1 — structural inversion

### Advantages amplified

- **Closed-loop discipline** becomes a moat because every run must produce evidence, decisions, artifacts, and next actions instead of idle text.
- **Thinking altitude** prevents both local optimization and empty strategy by requiring ascent to the governing system and descent to concrete action.
- **Control-layer focus** directs effort toward proof, eligibility, routing, and settlement mechanics where durable infrastructure advantage can exist.
- **Regenerative infrastructure** aligns commercial defensibility with market health and participant capability.
- **SOP structure** makes work auditable, repeatable, and improvable.

### Liabilities redesigned

- **Risk: theatrical overcomplexity.** Bound by Single Bottleneck Metric, one next action, and smallest sufficient intervention.
- **Risk: self-authorizing autonomy.** Bound by kernel authority, human sovereignty, grants, budget, evidence, and Consequence Gate.
- **Risk: abstract hegemony language.** Convert into lawful default infrastructure, accepted proof, interoperability, auditability, and participant welfare.
- **Risk: too many records.** Implement proportionally: issue first, then docs/schema only when the workflow is actually built.
- **Risk: founder-intent conflict with two-pass rule.** Preserve cognitive strengthening internally while repository-governed material decisions use exactly two explicit passes.

## Upward Pass 2 — adversarial compounding

Assume Pass 1 is deployed and the doctrine becomes widely used.

### New attacks

- The agent could optimize for beautiful doctrine instead of external validation.
- The information architecture could become bureaucratic and slow.
- The phrase "control layer" could drift toward coercive thinking.
- Multiple organs could duplicate RailScout logic locally.
- DALEOBANKS could accidentally absorb RailScout's refinery mission and confuse public distribution with business discovery.

### Strengthened design

- Primary metrics must privilege external signal, paid validation, reusable assets, and decision-quality improvement over document count.
- Any new RailScout databases, schemas, or workflows must be justified by a measured control advantage or repeated failure in the lighter system.
- Control-layer language must always be paired with legality, interoperability, due process, portability, auditability, and participant welfare.
- RailScout owns perception/evidence/refinery behavior; the kernel owns governance; DALEOBANKS owns public voice and distribution.
- Future implementation should add explicit boundary checks preventing DALEOBANKS from becoming the authority layer and preventing RailScout from bypassing the kernel.

## Decision

`EXPERIMENT`

Preserve this conversation as a founder-intent and doctrine record. Use it as the source input for a future RailScout organ doctrine PR, workflow template, and run-log schema. Do not grant new external-effect authority, production autonomy, spending authority, or status change from `planned` without an explicit reviewed change.

---

# Closed-loop SOP to implement later

RailScout serious-run SOP:

1. **Read canonical reality** — current north star, active opportunity, stage, SBM, prior decision, blockers, evidence, and queue.
2. **Determine authority** — founder decision, canonical docs, primary evidence, operating records, recent external evidence, secondary interpretation, assumptions.
3. **State operational objective** — what state change or decision is required and what counts as completion.
4. **Collect inputs** — only information needed for the objective.
5. **Separate truth classes** — verified fact, supported inference, working assumption, disputed claim, unresolved unknown.
6. **Map the system** — participants, incentives, money flows, authority, data, proof, dependencies, failures.
7. **Diagnose root constraint** — where value is trapped and what missing proof/trust/eligibility/routing/settlement layer governs it.
8. **Generate configurations** — software, service, diagnostic, certification, data exchange, proof layer, payment control, standard, partnership rail.
9. **Attack and strengthen** — apply advantage conversion and kernel-compatible two-pass governance for material decisions.
10. **Find strongest counterexample** — dead market, incumbent response, blocked regulation, no budget, substitute, or easier path.
11. **Rank survivors** — urgency, pain, budget, regulatory tailwind, evidence speed, capital intensity, data access, margin, defensibility, welfare.
12. **Backcast** — strongest end state → stage gates → current gate.
13. **Choose smallest consequential action** — safe, bounded, measurable, reversible where possible.
14. **Apply authority gate** — independent, notify, or founder approval required.
15. **Execute or stage** — act only within grants; otherwise prepare decision packet.
16. **Record artifact** — evidence, decision, diagnostic, interview guide, outreach, product spec, validation record, or SOP.
17. **Measure external result** — no response, rejection, objection, info, introduction, meeting, data access, pilot, payment, repeat use.
18. **Update thesis** — confidence, assumptions, disproof, unresolved unknowns.
19. **Route learning** — opportunity, claims ledger, decisions, SOP, risk controls, architecture primitives, founder review.
20. **Improve the system** — repair bad schema, unclear authority, missing evidence, duplicate work, or repeated failure.
21. **Queue exactly one next action** — no unbounded option cloud.

Compressed loop:

> Read → Orient → Diagnose → Design → Attack → Rank → Backcast → Act → Record → Measure → Learn → Improve → Queue → Repeat.

---

# RailScout thinking altitude ladder

1. **Raw reality:** What literally happened? What does the evidence say?
2. **Task:** What must be done next? Who owns it? What counts as complete?
3. **Workflow:** Where does the process break? Where do errors, rework, and exceptions accumulate?
4. **Product:** What tool/service removes the failure? What must the user see, enter, approve, or receive?
5. **Business model:** Who pays? What recurs? What improves retention and margin? Can cash conversion be structurally improved?
6. **Market structure:** Who controls access? Who benefits? Who blocks? Where does bargaining power sit?
7. **Control rail:** Who defines valid participation, proof, eligibility, routing, completion, and settlement?
8. **Regenerative market operating system:** Does the system make legitimate participants more capable, trusted, eligible, liquid, and coordinated?
9. **Portfolio/refinery architecture:** What did this teach the entire refinery? What should be reused, killed, or improved?

Core rule:

> Ascend until the governing system is visible. Descend until someone can take a concrete action.

---

# RailScout failure-mode handling

- **Execution failure:** repair artifact/action and retest.
- **Evidence failure:** lower confidence and collect stronger evidence.
- **Configuration failure:** redesign buyer, wedge, pricing, channel, proof, or product.
- **Market failure:** kill opportunity and preserve lesson.
- **System failure:** repair SOP, schema, metric, authority rule, agent instruction, or quality gate.

---

# Primary metrics

- Validated Business Discovery Throughput.
- Profitable Validated Business Discovery Assets.
- Time from signal to test.
- Cost per falsified hypothesis.
- External signal rate.
- Paid-validation rate.
- Time from validation to revenue.
- Reusable asset conversion rate.
- Decision-reversal rate.
- Repeated-error rate.
- Value created per founder hour.

---

# Repository/organ implications

## Kernel

The kernel remains the canonical governance source. RailScout doctrine must consume kernel contracts, authority, provenance, and consequence gates.

## RailScout

RailScout remains an organ candidate / planned organ until a reviewed change updates status. This issue strengthens its doctrine but does not create a repository or grant autonomy.

## DALEOBANKS

DALEOBANKS remains the public voice and distribution organ. It may distribute or route opportunities but must not absorb RailScout's founder-intelligence/refinery mission or the kernel's governance authority.

## Future implementation candidates

- Create `docs/RAILSCOUT_LIVE_PLAYER_DOCTRINE.md` from this issue.
- Add RailScout run-log schema.
- Add RailScout validation-sprint template.
- Add RailScout opportunity-scoring template.
- Add explicit DALEOBANKS/RailScout/kernel boundary tests.
- Update organ registry only after founder-approved PR.

---

# Next action

Create a reviewed branch/PR that converts this issue into canonical docs and/or schemas only after file-level implementation scope is approved.

title: Build inert Part 2 loader, MCP/A2A boundaries, and containment
body:
## Outcome

Build Opus Maximus Part 2 as an inert, evidence-bounded contribution stacked on the current Part 1 branch.

This PR implements only the paths assigned by the frozen handoff:

- `moduleloader/`
- `boundary/`
- `containment/`
- `tests/unit/test_module_loader.py`
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_boundary.py`
- `tests/unit/test_a2a_boundary.py`
- `tests/unit/test_containment.py`

No Claude-owned, sealed, constitutional, authority, grant, router, discovery, manifest, closure, repair, or runtime path is changed.

## Frozen dependency

- Frozen bundle commit: `99163767f634115b3d7c331d87888df5484b92d8`
- Bundle digest: `fe1556048a9ca60f5956388adb9ddb81cbf060491b1fc8f38c6e2892e42d2c0c`
- Verified independently: all 36 manifest entries match their file SHA-256 values and the exact manifest bytes match the sealed bundle digest
- Part 2 parent: `310b0c8043c45ccb90dd56012e920f54d253441e`
- Commit: `58ec6682e5c55e1d9e04ec4779e8d4faa81367f5`

The four Part 2 schemas are read-only dependencies. Their exact sealed hashes are checked before use; drift fails closed.

## What is built

### Governed module loader

- Exact predeclared module, descriptor, and artifact allowlist
- Frozen capability-request validation
- Claude discovery `lookup` and attached `offers` checks
- Required lifecycle verbs: inspect, validate, install, attach, activate, pause, shadow, compare, replace, rollback, detach, export-state, import-state, archive, restore
- Content-addressed artifacts and state snapshots
- Qualified shadow comparison, predecessor preservation, rollback lineage, and append-only hash-chained lifecycle evidence
- Founder-authorized forced detach with no module veto
- `active` means eligibility only; candidate code is never imported or executed

### MCP and A2A boundaries

- Exact `1.0.0` envelope validation with no downgrade
- Authentication semantics remain separate from authority
- Shared HMAC identity must explicitly report `identity_is_isolated=false`
- Mandatory sender resolution, freshness checks, and replay recorder
- Capability requests resolve through discovery and consequence ceilings
- Output is an immutable `PROPOSAL` with `confers_authority=false` and `execution_eligible=false`
- No gate, grant, executor, tool, transport, or network primitive

### Containment

- Frozen tier vocabulary: `in_process`, `hardened_container`, `microvm`, `wasm_component`
- Exact enforcement labels, including `policy_only`
- Risk floors for internal-untrusted, foreign, generated, and external-consequence workloads
- Provider declarations are not proof
- Self-attestation and nonce replay are refused
- Fresh independent attestations are reverified at selection
- No workload launch
- Missing evidence returns schema-valid `UNAVAILABLE`, never a silent downgrade

## Evidence state

Four schema-valid evidence records claim only:

- `claimed_state: BUILT`
- `reality: IMPLEMENTED`
- `external_effects: 0`
- `authority_minted: false`

This PR does **not** claim EXERCISED, PROVEN, HARDENED, live protocol interoperability, real runtime isolation, durable crash recovery, external outcomes, or technology #25 closure.

## Verification

Local scratch preflight executed all focused functions and parameter groups:

- 35 passed
- 0 failed
- Python compile and AST parsing passed
- AST guards found no candidate dynamic import, execution, process-launch, or network primitive

The scratch image lacked the repository's pytest/jsonschema packages, so that preflight is not represented as canonical pytest evidence. GitHub CI is the controlling dependency-backed result.

## Known upstream counterevidence

Part 1 parent `310b0c8` reports:

- 601 passing
- 20 failing
- the same 20 failures are `CONTRADICTION-0001`, caused by the sealed Package 3 live `organs/*.manifest.yaml` corpus after approved organ growth
- handoff conformance remains 26/26

This PR does not edit the repair corpus or suppress those failures. Acceptance requires all focused Part 2 tests to pass and no new failure outside the preserved BLK-2 set.

## Authority invariant

Models reason. Agents propose. Authorized humans decide. Kernel validates authority. Bounded execution occurs elsewhere. Evidence is reconciled.

No lifecycle state, authenticated envelope, discovery advertisement, or containment decision creates authority.

## Rollback and kill conditions

Rollback is closing this unmerged draft PR or reverting its single commit. Existing Part 1 files remain untouched.

Stop promotion if:

- any changed path escapes the assigned ownership set;
- a frozen digest differs;
- a module can import/execute itself, mint authority, or veto detach;
- a boundary can authorize or execute;
